spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m3p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Controllers, InitLeader, NoneC, Total

\* A print-shop job spooler where one of several controllers is the leader.
\* The leader may crash silently (at most once); a surviving controller then
\* takes over via a term bump. Jobs move queued -> printing -> done, and the
\* invariant protects the fact that no job is ever created or lost in transit.
VARIABLES leader, term, crashedC, queued, printing, done

TypeOK == leader \in Controllers /\ term \in Nat /\ crashedC \in Controllers \cup {NoneC}
          /\ queued \in Nat /\ printing \in Nat /\ done \in Nat

Init == leader = InitLeader /\ term = 0 /\ crashedC = NoneC
        /\ queued = Total /\ printing = 0 /\ done = 0

\* The one silent crash allowed by the twist: a controller (leader or not)
\* stops responding, with no notification to anyone else.
Crash == crashedC = NoneC /\ \E c \in Controllers:
            crashedC' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, queued, printing, done>>

\* Failover: if the current leader turns out to be the crashed one, some
\* surviving controller takes over and bumps the term.
Failover == leader = crashedC /\ \E c \in Controllers \ {crashedC}:
                leader' = c /\ term' = term + 1
                /\ UNCHANGED <<crashedC, queued, printing, done>>

StartPrint == leader # crashedC /\ queued > 0
              /\ queued' = queued - 1 /\ printing' = printing + 1
              /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedC, done>>

FinishPrint == leader # crashedC /\ printing > 0
               /\ printing' = printing - 1 /\ done' = done + 1
               /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedC, queued>>

Next == Crash \/ Failover \/ StartPrint \/ FinishPrint

vars == <<leader, term, crashedC, queued, printing, done>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(Failover) /\ WF_vars(StartPrint) /\ WF_vars(FinishPrint)

\* Nothing is created or destroyed: every job is always accounted for.
JobsConserved == queued + printing + done = Total

AllJobsEventuallyDone == <>(done = Total)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
    InitLeader = c1
    NoneC = none
    Total = 3
INVARIANT JobsConserved
PROPERTY AllJobsEventuallyDone
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A neighborhood print shop runs a small job spooler cluster with several controller
boxes, one of which is designated the leader at any time. Customers' print jobs
arrive already queued; only the leader is trusted to move a job from the queue into
the printer and then mark it finished. At most one controller in the whole cluster
can crash silently during a run -- it simply stops acting, with no crash message
sent to anyone, and that controller could be the leader itself or a bystander. When
the crash happens to have hit the currently-designated leader, the surviving
controllers eventually notice that the leader is unresponsive and one of them takes
over, bumping the cluster's term counter so the takeover is unambiguous. The full
action set is: (1) Crash, in which some controller silently goes dark, an event
that can happen at most once for the whole run; (2) Failover, which fires only when
the designated leader is exactly the one that crashed, and hands leadership to a
surviving controller while incrementing the term; (3) StartPrint, in which the
current (non-crashed) leader pulls one job out of the queue and begins printing it;
and (4) FinishPrint, in which the current (non-crashed) leader completes a job that
was printing and marks it done. Every job that exists is always either sitting in
the queue, currently printing, or already finished -- the spooler must never
invent an extra job out of thin air and must never quietly drop one, even across a
leader crash and takeover.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state the number of queued jobs plus the number
of printing jobs plus the number of finished jobs equals the fixed total number of
jobs the shop started with.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every job that starts out queued is eventually finished, even
though one controller (possibly the leader) may crash silently partway through.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od3m9p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
CONSTANT Banks, MaxEpoch

\* An interbank settlement batch is run once per epoch. Banks vote to close
\* out the current epoch's batch; when every bank in the current membership
\* has voted, the batch is settled and reconfiguration bumps the epoch. The
\* twist is that a bank may lag (its vote arrives late) but never fails
\* outright, so membership never shrinks. The invariant guards the fact that
\* settlement -- an irreversible transfer of funds -- fires at most once
\* per epoch, by keeping an append-only log of every settlement performed
\* and checking that log never records the same epoch twice.
VARIABLES epoch, voted, settleLog, pending, members

SettledEpochs == {settleLog[i] : i \in DOMAIN settleLog}

TypeOK == epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch /\ voted \subseteq Banks
          /\ settleLog \in Seq(0..MaxEpoch) /\ pending \in BOOLEAN
          /\ members \subseteq Banks

Init == epoch = 0 /\ voted = {} /\ settleLog = <<>> /\ pending = FALSE
        /\ members = Banks

\* A bank casts its close-out vote for the current batch; slow banks simply
\* vote later than others, they never drop out of the membership set.
CastVote == pending = FALSE /\ \E b \in members \ voted:
                voted' = voted \cup {b}
                /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, settleLog, pending, members>>

\* Once every current member has voted, the batch becomes ready to settle.
Quiesce == pending = FALSE /\ voted = members /\ voted # {}
           /\ pending' = TRUE
           /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, voted, settleLog, members>>

\* Settlement is the irreversible action: money moves for this epoch's batch.
\* The guard checks the log; if the guard were ever bypassed, the log would
\* pick up a duplicate epoch entry and the invariant below would catch it.
Settle == pending = TRUE /\ epoch \notin SettledEpochs
          /\ settleLog' = Append(settleLog, epoch)
          /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, voted, pending, members>>

\* Reconfiguration: after settlement, the epoch advances and voting resets.
\* No bank ever truly fails here, only lags, so members stays fixed.
Reconfigure == pending = TRUE /\ epoch \in SettledEpochs /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
               /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ voted' = {} /\ pending' = FALSE
               /\ UNCHANGED <<settleLog, members>>

Next == CastVote \/ Quiesce \/ Settle \/ Reconfigure

vars == <<epoch, voted, settleLog, pending, members>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No epoch is ever settled twice: the append-only settlement log never
\* contains the same epoch number in two different positions.
NoDuplicateSettlement == \A i \in DOMAIN settleLog, j \in DOMAIN settleLog:
                            i # j => settleLog[i] # settleLog[j]
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Banks = {b1, b2, b3}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INVARIANT NoDuplicateSettlement
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A consortium of banks runs one interbank settlement batch per epoch. Every bank
that is a current member of the consortium must cast its close-out vote for the
batch before the batch can be considered ready; a member bank might be slow to
respond -- its vote simply arrives late -- but under this arrangement no bank
ever actually fails or gets ejected from membership, it only lags behind the
others. The full action set is: (1) CastVote, in which some member bank that
has not yet voted for the current epoch's batch casts its vote; (2) Quiesce,
which fires once every current member has voted, marking the batch as ready to
settle; (3) Settle, the irreversible transfer of funds for the current epoch's
batch, which appends the current epoch number to an append-only settlement log
and is guarded so it can only run once quiescence has been reached and the
current epoch does not already appear in that log; and (4) Reconfigure, which,
once the current epoch has been settled, advances the consortium to the next
epoch and resets the vote tally so a fresh round of voting can begin. Because
settlement moves real money, the consortium's entire safety story rests on the
guarantee that no epoch's batch is ever settled a second time, no matter how
many banks lag or how the voting interleaves.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The append-only settlement log never contains the same epoch
number in two different positions, i.e. every epoch's batch is settled at most
once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m8p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Regions, NoneR, ConfirmIds, TotalPlayers

\* A game lobby matchmaker uses hierarchical locking: it first grabs a coarse
\* region lock, then a fine per-pairing lock, before reserving two waiting
\* players into a match. When the pairing is done it fires off a confirm
\* message and releases both locks immediately, so a new pairing cycle can
\* start in a different region before the old confirm is actually delivered.
\* Confirms sit in an unordered set, so delivery can happen in any order --
\* the twist is that these messages can be reordered relative to send order.
\* The invariant protects conservation: every player is always accounted for
\* as waiting, mid-match, or fully matched, never created or lost.
VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLockHeld, waiting, matching, matched, pendingConfirms

TypeOK == coarseLock \in Regions \cup {NoneR} /\ fineLockHeld \in BOOLEAN
          /\ waiting \in Nat /\ matching \in Nat /\ matched \in Nat
          /\ pendingConfirms \subseteq ConfirmIds

Init == coarseLock = NoneR /\ fineLockHeld = FALSE /\ waiting = TotalPlayers
        /\ matching = 0 /\ matched = 0 /\ pendingConfirms = {}

\* Grab the coarse (region) lock; this is the outer level of the hierarchy.
AcquireCoarse == coarseLock = NoneR /\ waiting >= 2 /\ \E r \in Regions:
                    coarseLock' = r
                    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLockHeld, waiting, matching, matched, pendingConfirms>>

\* Grab the fine (per-pairing) lock inside the held region, and reserve two
\* waiting players into the in-progress matching pool.
AcquireFine == coarseLock # NoneR /\ fineLockHeld = FALSE /\ waiting >= 2
               /\ fineLockHeld' = TRUE /\ waiting' = waiting - 2 /\ matching' = matching + 2
               /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, matched, pendingConfirms>>

\* The pairing is decided; a confirm message is sent and both locks are
\* released right away, letting a fresh region/pairing cycle start elsewhere
\* before this confirm is ever delivered.
SendConfirm == coarseLock # NoneR /\ fineLockHeld = TRUE
               /\ \E id \in ConfirmIds \ pendingConfirms:
                    pendingConfirms' = pendingConfirms \cup {id}
               /\ fineLockHeld' = FALSE /\ coarseLock' = NoneR
               /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, matching, matched>>

\* Confirms are delivered out of order from an unordered set: any pending
\* confirm, not just the oldest one, can be picked up next.
DeliverConfirm == \E id \in pendingConfirms:
                    pendingConfirms' = pendingConfirms \ {id}
                    /\ matching >= 2 /\ matching' = matching - 2 /\ matched' = matched + 2
                    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLockHeld, waiting>>

Next == AcquireCoarse \/ AcquireFine \/ SendConfirm \/ DeliverConfirm

vars == <<coarseLock, fineLockHeld, waiting, matching, matched, pendingConfirms>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(AcquireCoarse) /\ WF_vars(AcquireFine)
        /\ WF_vars(SendConfirm) /\ WF_vars(DeliverConfirm)

\* Nothing is created or destroyed: every player is waiting, mid-match, or
\* matched, and the three pools always sum to the fixed player total.
PlayersConserved == waiting + matching + matched = TotalPlayers

AllPlayersEventuallyMatched == <>(matched = TotalPlayers)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Regions = {r1, r2}
    NoneR = noner
    ConfirmIds = {1, 2, 3}
    TotalPlayers = 4
INVARIANT PlayersConserved
PROPERTY AllPlayersEventuallyMatched
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A multiplayer game's lobby matchmaker organizes waiting players into two-person
matches using a two-level locking scheme. To start a pairing attempt, the
matchmaker must first acquire a coarse lock on an entire lobby region, and only
once it holds that region can it acquire the finer-grained lock that actually
protects a single pairing attempt within that region. Once both locks are held
and two waiting players have been reserved into an in-progress "matching" pool,
the matchmaker fires off an asynchronous confirm message announcing that the
pairing is finalized, and immediately releases both the fine lock and the
coarse lock so the region is free for the next pairing attempt -- even before
that confirm message has actually been delivered. Confirm messages sit in an
unordered mailbox rather than a first-in-first-out queue, so they can be
delivered in any order relative to when they were sent; a confirm from a later
pairing cycle might be processed before one sent earlier. The full action set
is: (1) AcquireCoarse, which grabs the region-level lock whenever at least two
players are still waiting; (2) AcquireFine, which, once the coarse lock is
held, grabs the pairing-level lock and moves two waiting players into the
in-progress matching pool; (3) SendConfirm, which posts a new confirm message
to the mailbox and releases both locks; and (4) DeliverConfirm, which picks
any one pending confirm message out of the mailbox (not necessarily the
oldest) and finalizes that pairing, moving its two players from the matching
pool into the fully matched pool. Across all of this shuffling and reordering,
every player who ever entered the lobby must still be accounted for.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of players still
waiting plus the number of players mid-match plus the number of players fully
matched equals the fixed total number of players who entered the lobby.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every player who enters the waiting pool is eventually
moved into a fully matched pairing, even though confirm messages may be
delivered out of order.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m6p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Dispatchers, NoneD, MaxEpoch

\* An elevator bank in a skyscraper is put under the exclusive control of one
\* maintenance dispatcher at a time, via a time-limited lease tagged with an
\* epoch number. Only the current, unexpired lease holder may set the car's
\* pending destination. One dispatcher may crash silently mid-lease; the
\* invariant protects against exactly that: no destination is ever left
\* attributed to a dispatcher who is no longer the live, unexpired holder.
VARIABLES epoch, holder, leaseValid, crashedD, carSetBy

TypeOK == epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch /\ holder \in Dispatchers \cup {NoneD}
          /\ leaseValid \in BOOLEAN /\ crashedD \in Dispatchers \cup {NoneD}
          /\ carSetBy \in Dispatchers \cup {NoneD}

Init == epoch = 0 /\ holder = NoneD /\ leaseValid = FALSE
        /\ crashedD = NoneD /\ carSetBy = NoneD

\* A fresh lease is granted, at a new epoch, to some dispatcher that hasn't
\* crashed. Any pending car command from the previous lease is cleared.
Acquire == leaseValid = FALSE /\ epoch < MaxEpoch /\ \E d \in Dispatchers \ {crashedD}:
              holder' = d /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ leaseValid' = TRUE
              /\ carSetBy' = NoneD /\ UNCHANGED crashedD

\* The lease times out. Any car command issued under it is no longer trusted.
Expire == leaseValid = TRUE /\ leaseValid' = FALSE /\ carSetBy' = NoneD
          /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, crashedD>>

\* The one silent crash allowed by the twist: a dispatcher (holder or not)
\* stops responding without telling anyone. If it had a pending command in
\* flight, that command is voided since its author can no longer be trusted.
Crash == crashedD = NoneD /\ \E d \in Dispatchers:
            /\ crashedD' = d
            /\ carSetBy' = (IF carSetBy = d THEN NoneD ELSE carSetBy)
            /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, leaseValid>>

\* Only the current, unexpired, non-crashed holder may set a car destination.
Command == leaseValid = TRUE /\ holder # crashedD
           /\ carSetBy' = holder
           /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, leaseValid, crashedD>>

Next == Acquire \/ Expire \/ Crash \/ Command

vars == <<epoch, holder, leaseValid, crashedD, carSetBy>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No standing car command is ever attributed to anyone but the live,
\* unexpired, non-crashed lease holder -- an unauthorized or stale
\* dispatcher's command can never be the one in effect.
CommandsAreAuthorized == carSetBy # NoneD =>
                            (carSetBy = holder /\ leaseValid = TRUE /\ carSetBy # crashedD)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Dispatchers = {d1, d2, d3}
    NoneD = noned
    MaxEpoch = 3
INVARIANT CommandsAreAuthorized
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank is placed under maintenance control by one
dispatcher at a time. Control is granted as a time-limited lease stamped with
an increasing epoch number, and only the dispatcher currently holding a live,
unexpired lease is allowed to set the car's pending destination floor. At most
one dispatcher in the whole building can crash silently during a maintenance
session -- it simply goes unresponsive with no warning to anyone, and it might
be the current lease holder or an idle dispatcher waiting its turn. The full
action set is: (1) Acquire, which grants a brand-new lease, at a freshly
incremented epoch, to any dispatcher that has not crashed, but only once the
previous lease has already expired, and which clears out any car destination
left over from the prior lease; (2) Expire, which lets the current lease time
out, immediately voiding any destination command that was set under it; (3)
Crash, the one silent failure the twist allows, in which some dispatcher goes
dark, and if that dispatcher happened to be the one whose command is currently
in effect, that command is voided since its author can no longer be trusted to
still be legitimate; and (4) Command, in which the dispatcher currently holding
a live, unexpired lease -- provided it has not itself silently crashed -- sets
the car's pending destination floor. The building's safety depends entirely on
never letting a destination set by an unauthorized or stale dispatcher take
effect.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the elevator car has a pending destination set by
some dispatcher, that dispatcher must be exactly the current lease holder,
its lease must still be live and unexpired, and it must not be the dispatcher
that silently crashed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m9p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Bags, Slots, NoneS, MaxEpoch

\* An airport baggage router assigns bags to carousel slots. The routing
\* table is reconfigured in epochs: a reconfiguration clears every current
\* assignment and reopens all bags for (re)allocation under the new epoch.
\* The router itself may run slow -- it can lag behind the current epoch by
\* any amount, it just never actually fails -- but it must never allocate a
\* slot using stale, pre-reconfiguration information. The invariant protects
\* against two different bags ever holding the very same carousel slot.
VARIABLES epoch, assignedSlot, seenEpoch, pending

TypeOK == epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch /\ seenEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
          /\ assignedSlot \in [Bags -> Slots \cup {NoneS}]
          /\ pending \subseteq Bags

Init == epoch = 0 /\ seenEpoch = 0 /\ pending = Bags
        /\ assignedSlot = [b \in Bags |-> NoneS]

\* Reconfiguration: the routing table changes for a new epoch. Every current
\* slot assignment is released and every bag becomes pending again.
Reconfigure == epoch < MaxEpoch
               /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
               /\ assignedSlot' = [b \in Bags |-> NoneS]
               /\ pending' = Bags
               /\ UNCHANGED seenEpoch

\* The router is slow but never failed: it eventually notices each new
\* epoch, one increment at a time, however long it takes.
CatchUp == seenEpoch < epoch /\ seenEpoch' = seenEpoch + 1
           /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assignedSlot, pending>>

\* The router may only allocate once it has caught up to the current epoch
\* -- it must never assign a slot based on a stale epoch's routing table.
\* It picks a slot that is not currently held by any bag.
Allocate == seenEpoch = epoch /\ \E b \in pending: \E s \in Slots:
                (\A b2 \in Bags: assignedSlot[b2] # s)
                /\ assignedSlot' = [assignedSlot EXCEPT ![b] = s]
                /\ pending' = pending \ {b}
                /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, seenEpoch>>

\* A bag leaves the carousel area, freeing its slot for others.
Release == \E b \in Bags: assignedSlot[b] # NoneS
                /\ assignedSlot' = [assignedSlot EXCEPT ![b] = NoneS]
                /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, seenEpoch, pending>>

Next == Reconfigure \/ CatchUp \/ Allocate \/ Release

vars == <<epoch, assignedSlot, seenEpoch, pending>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(Reconfigure) /\ WF_vars(CatchUp) /\ WF_vars(Allocate)

\* No two distinct bags ever occupy the same carousel slot at once.
NoDoubleAllocation == \A b1 \in Bags, b2 \in Bags:
                        b1 # b2 => (assignedSlot[b1] = NoneS \/ assignedSlot[b2] = NoneS
                                    \/ assignedSlot[b1] # assignedSlot[b2])

AllPendingEventuallyAllocated == <>(pending = {})
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Bags = {bg1, bg2, bg3}
    Slots = {s1, s2, s3}
    NoneS = nones
    MaxEpoch = 2
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
PROPERTY AllPendingEventuallyAllocated
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airport's baggage router directs suitcases and bins onto carousel slots for
pickup. The router's assignment table is organized around numbered epochs: a
reconfiguration event (triggered, say, by a carousel going into maintenance
mode or a new flight bank being scheduled) bumps the epoch, releases every bag
currently holding a slot, and puts every bag back into the pool of bags
waiting to be assigned. The router hardware itself can run behind -- it may
take an arbitrarily long time to notice that a new epoch has started -- but it
never actually crashes or drops out of the system, it is only ever slow. The
full action set is: (1) Reconfigure, which advances the epoch counter,
clearing every current slot assignment and marking every bag as pending
again; (2) CatchUp, in which the (possibly lagging) router notices the next
epoch has begun and advances its own view of the epoch by one step, however
many steps behind it may currently be; (3) Allocate, in which the router --
but only once its own view of the epoch has fully caught up to the true
current epoch, so it never acts on stale routing information -- picks a bag
that is still pending and a carousel slot that is not currently held by any
bag, and assigns that bag to that slot; and (4) Release, in which a bag that
already has a slot leaves the carousel area, freeing its slot. Even though the
router can lag arbitrarily far behind and reconfigurations can wipe the board
clean at any time, the carousel must never end up with two different bags
claiming the exact same slot.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For any two distinct bags, they never simultaneously hold
the same carousel slot -- each slot is assigned to at most one bag at a time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag that becomes pending is eventually allocated a
carousel slot, even though the router may lag arbitrarily far behind the
current epoch before catching up.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m9p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Commands, MaxEpoch

\* A smart-home door lock network re-keys itself in numbered epochs. Each
\* emergency unlock command is a one-time token; the message carrying it can
\* be delivered late, dropped, or -- because the network's mesh radios do not
\* guarantee ordering -- redelivered as a stray duplicate after it already
\* took effect. The invariant protects the fact that redeeming a token is an
\* irreversible action: the physical bolt only ever retracts for a given
\* token once, no matter how the duplicate or reordered messages land.
VARIABLES epoch, inflight, consumeCount, appliedAtEpoch

TypeOK == epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch /\ inflight \subseteq Commands
          /\ consumeCount \in [Commands -> Nat]
          /\ appliedAtEpoch \in [Commands -> 0..MaxEpoch]

Init == epoch = 0 /\ inflight = {}
        /\ consumeCount = [c \in Commands |-> 0]
        /\ appliedAtEpoch = [c \in Commands |-> 0]

\* The network re-keys, advancing the epoch. Outstanding messages are
\* untouched by this -- they may still be delivered (or dropped) later,
\* regardless of which epoch they were originally sent under.
Reconfigure == epoch < MaxEpoch /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
               /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, consumeCount, appliedAtEpoch>>

\* A command token is (re-)sent over the mesh. The same token can be issued
\* again even after it was already redeemed, modeling a stray duplicate
\* radio message arriving out of order.
IssueToken == \E c \in Commands \ inflight:
                 inflight' = inflight \cup {c}
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, consumeCount, appliedAtEpoch>>

\* A pending message is delivered, and delivery order has no relation to
\* send order. The bolt only actually retracts the first time a given
\* token is redeemed; any later duplicate delivery is a no-op for the bolt.
Deliver == \E c \in inflight:
              /\ inflight' = inflight \ {c}
              /\ IF consumeCount[c] = 0
                 THEN /\ consumeCount' = [consumeCount EXCEPT ![c] = 1]
                      /\ appliedAtEpoch' = [appliedAtEpoch EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
                 ELSE UNCHANGED <<consumeCount, appliedAtEpoch>>
              /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* A pending message is lost in transit and never delivered at all.
Expire == \E c \in inflight: inflight' = inflight \ {c}
          /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, consumeCount, appliedAtEpoch>>

Next == Reconfigure \/ IssueToken \/ Deliver \/ Expire

vars == <<epoch, inflight, consumeCount, appliedAtEpoch>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every emergency unlock token redeems the bolt at most once, no matter
\* how many times its message is duplicated, delayed, or reordered.
AtMostOnce == \A c \in Commands: consumeCount[c] <= 1
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Commands = {t1, t2, t3}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INVARIANT AtMostOnce
nl:
A smart-home's networked door locks periodically re-key themselves, and each
re-keying event bumps a network-wide epoch counter. Separately, the household
issues one-time emergency unlock tokens over the same low-power mesh radio
that carries the re-keying traffic; the mesh gives no ordering guarantee at
all, so a token's unlock message can be delayed, dropped outright, or -- worst
of all -- redelivered as a stray duplicate well after it already caused the
bolt to retract. The full action set is: (1) Reconfigure, in which the
network re-keys and advances the epoch counter, without touching any messages
that are still in flight; (2) IssueToken, in which some emergency token not
currently in flight gets sent out over the mesh, including tokens that were
already redeemed earlier -- a duplicate transmission of an old message; (3)
Deliver, in which some pending message is picked up off the mesh (delivery
order bears no relation to send order) and, if that token has never yet
retracted the bolt, the bolt retracts and the token is marked redeemed at the
current epoch, but if the token was already redeemed, this delivery is
silently absorbed as a harmless duplicate with no further effect; and (4)
Expire, in which a pending message is simply lost and never delivered. No
matter how many times a token's message is duplicated or how badly the
delivery order is scrambled relative to when messages were sent, retracting
the bolt for a given token is something that can only ever really happen
once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every emergency unlock token, the number of times its
redemption has actually retracted the bolt is never more than one.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m5p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANT Instances, Voters, Quorum

\* A network of vending machines is organized into two independent machine
\* clusters (Instances) that both draw from one shared physical resource --
\* a single coin-change hopper -- so only one cluster may actually be
\* dispensing from it at a time. Before a cluster may take the hopper, a
\* quorum of independent voting controllers must approve its request. The
\* invariant is classic mutual exclusion: the two clusters can never both
\* hold the shared hopper at once.
VARIABLES active, requesting, votes, everGranted

TypeOK == active \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN] /\ requesting \subseteq Instances
          /\ votes \in [Instances -> SUBSET Voters]
          /\ everGranted \subseteq Instances

Init == active = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE] /\ requesting = {}
        /\ votes = [i \in Instances |-> {}] /\ everGranted = {}

\* A cluster opens a fresh voting round for the shared hopper, but only
\* while no cluster currently holds it.
Request(i) == ~active[i] /\ i \notin requesting /\ (\A j \in Instances: ~active[j])
              /\ requesting' = requesting \cup {i} /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![i] = {}]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<active, everGranted>>

\* An independent controller casts its vote in favor of a cluster's request.
VoteFor(i) == i \in requesting /\ \E v \in Voters \ votes[i]:
                 votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![i] = @ \cup {v}]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<active, requesting, everGranted>>

\* Once quorum is reached and the hopper is still free, the cluster is
\* granted exclusive use of it.
Grant(i) == i \in requesting /\ (\A j \in Instances: ~active[j])
            /\ Cardinality(votes[i]) >= Quorum
            /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
            /\ requesting' = requesting \ {i}
            /\ everGranted' = everGranted \cup {i}
            /\ UNCHANGED votes

\* The cluster finishes dispensing change and releases the shared hopper.
Release(i) == active[i] /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<requesting, votes, everGranted>>

Next == \E i \in Instances: Request(i) \/ VoteFor(i) \/ Grant(i) \/ Release(i)

vars == <<active, requesting, votes, everGranted>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A i \in Instances: SF_vars(Request(i)) /\ SF_vars(VoteFor(i))
                               /\ SF_vars(Grant(i)) /\ SF_vars(Release(i))

\* Mutual exclusion: the two independent clusters never both hold the one
\* shared hopper at the same time.
Mutex == \A i \in Instances, j \in Instances: i # j => ~(active[i] /\ active[j])

EventuallyBothServed == <>(everGranted = Instances)

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {i1, i2}
    Voters = {v1, v2, v3}
    Quorum = 2
INVARIANT Mutex
PROPERTY EventuallyBothServed
nl:
A regional vending machine network is split into two independent operating
clusters, each one managing its own bank of machines, but both clusters share
a single physical coin-and-change hopper that neither can do without: only one
cluster may actually be drawing change from the shared hopper at any given
moment. Before a cluster is allowed to take control of the hopper, it must
first open a fresh voting round and collect approval from a quorum of the
network's independent controller nodes; a single controller's vote by itself
is not enough. The full action set is: (1) Request, in which a cluster opens
a new voting round for the shared hopper, but only if the hopper is currently
held by neither cluster; (2) VoteFor, in which one of the independent
controllers casts its approval vote for whichever cluster currently has an
open voting round; (3) Grant, in which, once a cluster's open round has
collected votes from at least a quorum of controllers and the hopper is still
held by no one, that cluster is handed exclusive control of the hopper; and
(4) Release, in which a cluster that currently holds the hopper gives it back
up, freeing it for the other cluster's next request. Because the two clusters
are otherwise completely independent systems that happen to share this one
piece of hardware, the network's whole safety story rests on never letting
both clusters hold the hopper at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The two independent vending clusters are never both holding
the shared coin hopper at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Both independent clusters eventually get at least one turn
holding the shared hopper, even though they are competing for exclusive
access to the very same piece of hardware.

---- MODULE W4Od10m8p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Routes, NoneR, TotalTrains, MaxLag

\* A subway signalling block system uses hierarchical locking: a train must
\* first claim a coarse route lock, then the fine-grained signal block lock,
\* before it may enter the block. Releasing the block hierarchy requires an
\* acknowledgement from the line's signalling controller, which can be
\* arbitrarily slow to respond (it never actually fails, it just lags). The
\* invariant protects conservation: every train is always accounted for as
\* waiting, occupying a block, or having arrived, never created or lost.
VARIABLES routeLock, blockHeld, waiting, inBlock, arrived, ctrlLag

TypeOK == routeLock \in Routes \cup {NoneR} /\ blockHeld \in BOOLEAN
          /\ waiting \in Nat /\ inBlock \in Nat /\ arrived \in Nat
          /\ ctrlLag \in 0..MaxLag

Init == routeLock = NoneR /\ blockHeld = FALSE /\ waiting = TotalTrains
        /\ inBlock = 0 /\ arrived = 0 /\ ctrlLag = 0

\* Claim the coarse, route-level lock -- the outer level of the hierarchy.
AcquireRoute == routeLock = NoneR /\ waiting >= 1 /\ \E r \in Routes:
                   routeLock' = r
                /\ UNCHANGED <<blockHeld, waiting, inBlock, arrived, ctrlLag>>

\* Claim the fine, signal-block lock inside the held route, and let one
\* waiting train enter the block. This starts the controller's countdown
\* to eventually acknowledge this train's release -- however long it takes.
AcquireBlockAndEnter == routeLock # NoneR /\ blockHeld = FALSE /\ waiting >= 1
                         /\ blockHeld' = TRUE /\ waiting' = waiting - 1 /\ inBlock' = inBlock + 1
                         /\ \E lag \in 1..MaxLag: ctrlLag' = lag
                         /\ UNCHANGED <<routeLock, arrived>>

\* The signalling controller is slow but never failed: it keeps working
\* down its own backlog, one tick at a time, however long that takes.
CtrlTick == ctrlLag > 0 /\ ctrlLag' = ctrlLag - 1
            /\ UNCHANGED <<routeLock, blockHeld, waiting, inBlock, arrived>>

\* Once the controller has fully caught up, the train completes its run
\* through the block and both locks are released for the next train.
AckRelease == blockHeld = TRUE /\ ctrlLag = 0 /\ inBlock >= 1
              /\ blockHeld' = FALSE /\ routeLock' = NoneR
              /\ inBlock' = inBlock - 1 /\ arrived' = arrived + 1
              /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, ctrlLag>>

Next == AcquireRoute \/ AcquireBlockAndEnter \/ CtrlTick \/ AckRelease

vars == <<routeLock, blockHeld, waiting, inBlock, arrived, ctrlLag>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(AcquireRoute) /\ WF_vars(AcquireBlockAndEnter)
        /\ WF_vars(CtrlTick) /\ WF_vars(AckRelease)

\* Nothing is created or destroyed: every train is waiting, occupying a
\* signalled block, or arrived, and the three counts always sum to the
\* fixed number of trains that entered the line.
TrainsConserved == waiting + inBlock + arrived = TotalTrains

AllTrainsEventuallyArrive == <>(arrived = TotalTrains)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Routes = {r1, r2}
    NoneR = noner
    TotalTrains = 3
    MaxLag = 2
INVARIANT TrainsConserved
PROPERTY AllTrainsEventuallyArrive
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway line's signalling system protects its track using two levels of
locking. Before any train can move into a signal block, the signalling logic
must first claim a coarse lock on the whole route the block belongs to, and
only then claim the finer-grained lock on that specific signal block itself.
Once a train is let into the block, releasing the block hierarchy back for
the next train is not automatic -- it requires an acknowledgement from the
line's signalling controller, and that controller can be arbitrarily slow to
send its acknowledgement (it might take one tick or a dozen), but it never
actually fails or stops working entirely, it always eventually gets there.
The full action set is: (1) AcquireRoute, which claims the coarse route-level
lock whenever at least one train is still waiting to depart; (2)
AcquireBlockAndEnter, which, once the route lock is held, claims the block-
level lock and lets one waiting train enter the signal block, kicking off
the controller's countdown -- of unknown but finite length -- toward
eventually acknowledging this train's release; (3) CtrlTick, in which the
slow-but-never-failed controller works its countdown down by one step; and
(4) AckRelease, which fires only once the controller's countdown has fully
reached zero, and which lets the train complete its run through the block,
releases both the route and block locks, and moves that train into the
arrived count. No matter how long the controller's countdown runs before it
acknowledges each release, every train that ever set out must still be
accounted for somewhere in the system.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of trains still
waiting plus the number of trains currently occupying a signalled block plus
the number of trains that have arrived equals the fixed total number of
trains that set out on the line.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every train that sets out eventually arrives, even though
the signalling controller's acknowledgement can be arbitrarily slow before
each release.

---- MODULE W4Od9m7p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Controllers, AdminId, NoneC, MaxVersion

\* A power-grid load shedder guards its emergency trip -- an irreversible
\* breaker action that sheds load for a region -- behind a compare-and-swap
\* register. A normal controller must first read the register's version and
\* can only trip if its cached version still matches (a genuine CAS), since
\* routine grid reconfiguration events can bump the version and make a
\* controller's cached copy stale. A privileged admin may instead force the
\* trip, bypassing the version check entirely -- but even the admin's
\* override still must respect the fact that the trip can only ever happen
\* once. The invariant protects exactly that irreversible-once guarantee.
VARIABLES version, normalCached, tripCount, trippedBy

TypeOK == version \in 0..MaxVersion /\ normalCached \in 0..MaxVersion
          /\ tripCount \in Nat /\ trippedBy \in Controllers \cup {AdminId, NoneC}

Init == version = 0 /\ normalCached = 0 /\ tripCount = 0 /\ trippedBy = NoneC

\* A normal controller (re)reads the current register version into its cache.
ReadVersion == normalCached' = version /\ UNCHANGED <<version, tripCount, trippedBy>>

\* Routine, trip-unrelated grid reconfiguration bumps the shared register's
\* version, which can leave a controller's earlier cached read stale.
GridTick == version < MaxVersion /\ version' = version + 1
            /\ UNCHANGED <<normalCached, tripCount, trippedBy>>

\* A normal controller's compare-and-swap only succeeds if its cached
\* version still matches the live register and the trip hasn't fired yet.
NormalCAS == normalCached = version /\ tripCount = 0 /\ \E c \in Controllers:
                trippedBy' = c
             /\ tripCount' = tripCount + 1 /\ version' = version + 1
             /\ UNCHANGED normalCached

\* The privileged admin can force the trip without matching any version,
\* but still only while it has not already happened.
AdminOverride == tripCount = 0 /\ trippedBy' = AdminId
                 /\ tripCount' = tripCount + 1 /\ version' = version + 1
                 /\ UNCHANGED normalCached

Next == ReadVersion \/ GridTick \/ NormalCAS \/ AdminOverride

vars == <<version, normalCached, tripCount, trippedBy>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The irreversible load-shed trip -- whether performed by a normal
\* controller's successful compare-and-swap or by the admin's override --
\* happens at most once, no matter how the version register is bumped by
\* unrelated grid events in between.
AtMostOnceTrip == tripCount <= 1
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2}
    AdminId = admin
    NoneC = nonec
    MaxVersion = 4
INVARIANT AtMostOnceTrip
nl:
A regional power grid's automated load shedder holds one truly irreversible
button: an emergency trip that sheds load across a whole region's breakers.
To keep two controllers from ever triggering it independently and unsafely,
the trip is gated by a compare-and-swap version register. A normal grid
controller must first read the register's current version into its own
cache; later, its attempt to trip only actually succeeds if its cached
version still matches whatever the register currently holds -- if the
register moved on in the meantime (say, because of routine grid
reconfiguration unrelated to the trip itself), the controller's cached
version is stale and its attempt is simply not eligible to succeed. Separately,
a privileged admin account is allowed to force the trip directly, skipping
the version check entirely -- but even the admin's override still must never
let the trip fire more than the one time it is allowed to. The full action
set is: (1) ReadVersion, in which a normal controller refreshes its cached
copy of the register's current version; (2) GridTick, in which the register's
version advances due to routine, trip-unrelated grid reconfiguration events;
(3) NormalCAS, in which a normal controller's cache still matches the live
register and the trip has not yet occurred, so its compare-and-swap succeeds,
firing the trip and recording which controller did it; and (4)
AdminOverride, in which the privileged admin forces the trip directly,
without needing any matching cached version, provided the trip has not
already occurred. No matter how the version register gets bumped around by
unrelated events, and no matter whether a normal controller or the admin
ends up being the one to do it, the region's load-shedding trip can only
ever really happen once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of times the irreversible load-shedding trip has
actually fired is never more than one, whether it was triggered by a normal
controller's compare-and-swap or by the admin's privileged override.

---- MODULE W4Od16m5p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANT Prescriptions, Voters, Quorum

\* A pharmacy's automated dispenser only releases a controlled-substance
\* prescription once a quorum of independent pharmacist-review systems has
\* voted to approve it. Approval votes travel as separate messages that are
\* first sent and only later delivered into the running tally, and the
\* channel gives no ordering guarantee -- votes (and their retries) can be
\* delivered, or lost, in any order relative to when they were sent. The
\* invariant protects the fact that dispensing is irreversible: once a
\* prescription is dispensed, it can never be dispensed again.
VARIABLES sentVotes, appliedVotes, dispenseCount, everDispensed

TypeOK == sentVotes \subseteq (Prescriptions \X Voters)
          /\ appliedVotes \in [Prescriptions -> SUBSET Voters]
          /\ dispenseCount \in [Prescriptions -> Nat]
          /\ everDispensed \subseteq Prescriptions

Init == sentVotes = {} /\ appliedVotes = [p \in Prescriptions |-> {}]
        /\ dispenseCount = [p \in Prescriptions |-> 0] /\ everDispensed = {}

\* A pharmacist-review system sends its approval vote for a prescription.
SendVote(p, v) == <<p, v>> \notin sentVotes
                  /\ sentVotes' = sentVotes \cup {<<p, v>>}
                  /\ UNCHANGED <<appliedVotes, dispenseCount, everDispensed>>

\* A pending vote is delivered into the running tally -- delivery order has
\* no relation to send order.
DeliverVote(p, v) == <<p, v>> \in sentVotes
                     /\ sentVotes' = sentVotes \ {<<p, v>>}
                     /\ appliedVotes' = [appliedVotes EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {v}]
                     /\ UNCHANGED <<dispenseCount, everDispensed>>

\* A pending vote is simply lost in transit, never delivered.
ExpireVote(p, v) == <<p, v>> \in sentVotes
                    /\ sentVotes' = sentVotes \ {<<p, v>>}
                    /\ UNCHANGED <<appliedVotes, dispenseCount, everDispensed>>

\* Once a prescription's tally has reached quorum, and only if it has never
\* been dispensed before, the dispenser releases it -- this can only ever
\* happen the one time.
Dispense(p) == dispenseCount[p] = 0 /\ Cardinality(appliedVotes[p]) >= Quorum
               /\ dispenseCount' = [dispenseCount EXCEPT ![p] = 1]
               /\ everDispensed' = everDispensed \cup {p}
               /\ UNCHANGED <<sentVotes, appliedVotes>>

Next == (\E p \in Prescriptions, v \in Voters: SendVote(p, v) \/ DeliverVote(p, v) \/ ExpireVote(p, v))
        \/ (\E p \in Prescriptions: Dispense(p))

vars == <<sentVotes, appliedVotes, dispenseCount, everDispensed>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ (\A p \in Prescriptions, v \in Voters: SF_vars(SendVote(p, v)) /\ SF_vars(DeliverVote(p, v)))
        /\ (\A p \in Prescriptions: SF_vars(Dispense(p)))

\* No prescription is ever dispensed more than once, no matter how its
\* approval votes are delayed, dropped, or delivered out of order.
AtMostOnceDispensed == \A p \in Prescriptions: dispenseCount[p] <= 1

AllPrescriptionsEventuallyDispensed == <>(everDispensed = Prescriptions)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Prescriptions = {p1, p2}
    Voters = {v1, v2, v3}
    Quorum = 2
INVARIANT AtMostOnceDispensed
PROPERTY AllPrescriptionsEventuallyDispensed
nl:
A pharmacy's automated dispensing cabinet will only release a controlled-
substance prescription once a quorum of independent pharmacist-review systems
has approved it. Each review system's approval is sent as a separate message
that travels to the dispenser's tally over a channel that gives absolutely no
delivery-order guarantee: approval messages (and any retried copies of them)
can be delivered late, delivered early relative to when other approvals were
sent, or simply lost outright. The full action set is: (1) SendVote, in
which some pharmacist-review system sends its approval message for some
prescription that it does not currently have a message already in flight
for; (2) DeliverVote, in which some pending approval message is picked up
off the channel -- in no particular order relative to when messages were
sent -- and recorded into that prescription's running tally; (3)
ExpireVote, in which a pending approval message is simply lost in transit
and never recorded; and (4) Dispense, in which, once a prescription's tally
has reached the required quorum of approvals and that prescription has never
been dispensed before, the cabinet releases it. No matter how badly the
approval messages get shuffled, delayed, or dropped along the way, a given
prescription can only ever be dispensed the one time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No prescription is ever dispensed more than once, no matter
how its approval votes are reordered, delayed, or dropped in transit.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every prescription eventually gets dispensed, even though
its approval votes may be delivered out of order or occasionally lost along
the way.

---- MODULE W4Od1m0p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Aircraft, Slots, NoneS, MaxVersion, MaxRetries

\* An air-traffic runway allocator hands out landing slots using optimistic
\* locking: a controller first snapshots a slot's version number, and its
\* later commit only succeeds if that version has not moved and the slot is
\* still free -- otherwise the attempt simply fails and must be retried from
\* a fresh snapshot. Snapshot-and-commit messages are not delivered in send
\* order, so several aircraft's attempts for different (or the same) slots
\* can be resolved in any order. The invariant protects against two
\* different aircraft ever holding the very same runway slot.
VARIABLES assignedSlot, slotVersion, readCache, retries

TypeOK == assignedSlot \in [Aircraft -> Slots \cup {NoneS}]
          /\ slotVersion \in [Slots -> 0..MaxVersion]
          /\ readCache \subseteq (Aircraft \X Slots \X (0..MaxVersion))
          /\ retries \in [Aircraft -> 0..MaxRetries]

Init == assignedSlot = [a \in Aircraft |-> NoneS]
        /\ slotVersion = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
        /\ readCache = {} /\ retries = [a \in Aircraft |-> 0]

\* Bounded counters saturate at their cap instead of growing forever or
\* blocking progress once the cap is reached.
BumpTo(v, cap) == IF v < cap THEN v + 1 ELSE v
Bump(v) == BumpTo(v, MaxVersion)

\* A controller, for an aircraft with no current slot, snapshots a slot's
\* live version number for a later optimistic commit attempt.
StartRead(a, s) == assignedSlot[a] = NoneS
                   /\ ~(\E s2 \in Slots, v2 \in 0..MaxVersion: <<a, s2, v2>> \in readCache)
                   /\ readCache' = readCache \cup {<<a, s, slotVersion[s]>>}
                   /\ UNCHANGED <<assignedSlot, slotVersion, retries>>

\* The commit succeeds only if the snapshotted version still matches the
\* live register and no other aircraft currently holds that slot.
CommitSuccess(a, s, v) == <<a, s, v>> \in readCache /\ v = slotVersion[s]
                          /\ (\A a2 \in Aircraft: assignedSlot[a2] # s)
                          /\ readCache' = readCache \ {<<a, s, v>>}
                          /\ assignedSlot' = [assignedSlot EXCEPT ![a] = s]
                          /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![s] = Bump(v)]
                          /\ UNCHANGED retries

\* The commit fails -- the snapshot went stale or the slot is already
\* taken -- and the attempt is simply dropped; the controller must retry
\* with a fresh snapshot.
CommitFail(a, s, v) == <<a, s, v>> \in readCache
                       /\ ~(v = slotVersion[s] /\ (\A a2 \in Aircraft: assignedSlot[a2] # s))
                       /\ readCache' = readCache \ {<<a, s, v>>}
                       /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![a] = BumpTo(@, MaxRetries)]
                       /\ UNCHANGED <<assignedSlot, slotVersion>>

\* An aircraft that already holds a slot gives it up; the version bumps so
\* any other aircraft's stale outstanding snapshot for that slot is voided.
Release(a) == assignedSlot[a] # NoneS
              /\ assignedSlot' = [assignedSlot EXCEPT ![a] = NoneS]
              /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![assignedSlot[a]] = Bump(@)]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<readCache, retries>>

Next == (\E a \in Aircraft, s \in Slots: StartRead(a, s))
        \/ (\E a \in Aircraft, s \in Slots, v \in 0..MaxVersion: CommitSuccess(a, s, v) \/ CommitFail(a, s, v))
        \/ (\E a \in Aircraft: Release(a))

vars == <<assignedSlot, slotVersion, readCache, retries>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No two distinct aircraft ever hold the same runway slot at once, no
\* matter how snapshot-and-commit attempts get reordered or retried.
NoDoubleAllocation == \A a1 \in Aircraft, a2 \in Aircraft:
                         a1 # a2 /\ assignedSlot[a1] # NoneS => assignedSlot[a1] # assignedSlot[a2]
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Aircraft = {p1, p2}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    NoneS = nones
    MaxVersion = 2
    MaxRetries = 2
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
An air-traffic control system allocates landing slots on a shared runway
schedule using optimistic locking rather than heavyweight locking: instead of
holding a lock while it decides, a controller working on behalf of some
aircraft first takes a snapshot of a slot's current version number, works out
whether the slot looks free, and only later attempts to commit that decision.
The commit is only honored if the slot's version has not moved since the
snapshot was taken and no other aircraft currently holds the slot; otherwise
the attempt is simply rejected and the controller must go back and take a
fresh snapshot to retry. Because these snapshot and commit messages travel
independently and are not guaranteed to arrive in the order they were sent,
several aircraft's attempts -- for the same slot or different ones -- can be
resolved in essentially any order. The full action set is: (1) StartRead, in
which a controller for an aircraft that currently holds no slot takes a fresh
snapshot of some slot's live version number; (2) CommitSuccess, in which a
previously taken snapshot is acted on, and because its version still matches
the slot's live version and no aircraft currently holds that slot, the
aircraft is assigned the slot and the slot's version is bumped; (3)
CommitFail, in which a previously taken snapshot is acted on but is found to
be stale (the version moved) or the slot is already taken, so the attempt is
simply discarded and the controller's retry count for that aircraft goes up;
and (4) Release, in which an aircraft that holds a slot gives it up, which
also bumps that slot's version so that any other aircraft's outstanding
stale snapshot for it is invalidated. No matter how many attempts race each
other or how their snapshot-and-commit messages get reordered, two different
aircraft must never end up holding the exact same runway slot.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct aircraft ever hold the same runway slot at
the same time, no matter how snapshot-and-commit messages for optimistic
locking attempts are reordered or retried.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m7p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Capacity, InitPendingA, InitPendingB

\* Two independent airport baggage-router instances -- one per terminal --
\* feed bags into a single shared sorting buffer of bounded capacity. Each
\* instance decides whether it is safe to add a bag by first reading the
\* buffer's shared occupancy register, then only committing that addition
\* via a compare-and-swap that succeeds solely if the register still matches
\* what it read. The invariant protects the shared buffer's bounded
\* capacity, which the two otherwise-unrelated instances must never together
\* exceed.
VARIABLES sharedCount, pendingA, pendingB, cachedA, cachedB

TypeOK == sharedCount \in 0..Capacity /\ pendingA \in Nat /\ pendingB \in Nat
          /\ cachedA \in 0..Capacity /\ cachedB \in 0..Capacity

Init == sharedCount = 0 /\ pendingA = InitPendingA /\ pendingB = InitPendingB
        /\ cachedA = 0 /\ cachedB = 0

\* Terminal A's router refreshes its cached view of the shared register.
ReadA == cachedA' = sharedCount /\ UNCHANGED <<sharedCount, pendingA, pendingB, cachedB>>

\* Terminal A's compare-and-swap only succeeds if its cached read is still
\* fresh and showed room in the shared buffer.
CasA == pendingA > 0 /\ cachedA = sharedCount /\ cachedA < Capacity
        /\ sharedCount' = sharedCount + 1 /\ pendingA' = pendingA - 1
        /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingB, cachedA, cachedB>>

\* Terminal B's router refreshes its cached view of the shared register.
ReadB == cachedB' = sharedCount /\ UNCHANGED <<sharedCount, pendingA, pendingB, cachedA>>

\* Terminal B's compare-and-swap only succeeds if its cached read is still
\* fresh and showed room in the shared buffer.
CasB == pendingB > 0 /\ cachedB = sharedCount /\ cachedB < Capacity
        /\ sharedCount' = sharedCount + 1 /\ pendingB' = pendingB - 1
        /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingA, cachedA, cachedB>>

\* Downstream sorting removes a bag from the shared buffer, freeing a slot
\* that either terminal's instance may then claim.
Remove == sharedCount > 0 /\ sharedCount' = sharedCount - 1
          /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingA, pendingB, cachedA, cachedB>>

Next == ReadA \/ CasA \/ ReadB \/ CasB \/ Remove

vars == <<sharedCount, pendingA, pendingB, cachedA, cachedB>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ SF_vars(ReadA) /\ SF_vars(CasA) /\ SF_vars(ReadB) /\ SF_vars(CasB) /\ SF_vars(Remove)

\* The shared buffer's occupancy never exceeds its fixed capacity, no
\* matter how the two independent terminal instances race to fill it.
BoundedCapacity == sharedCount <= Capacity

AllBagsEventuallyPlaced == <>(pendingA = 0 /\ pendingB = 0)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Capacity = 2
    InitPendingA = 2
    InitPendingB = 2
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
PROPERTY AllBagsEventuallyPlaced
nl:
An airport runs two baggage-router instances that are otherwise completely
independent systems -- one dedicated to Terminal A's flights, one to Terminal
B's -- yet both instances feed newly-arriving bags into one single shared
sorting buffer of strictly bounded capacity. Neither instance is allowed to
just push a bag into the shared buffer on faith; each must first read the
buffer's shared occupancy register to see its current level, and its
decision to actually add a bag only takes effect through a compare-and-swap
that succeeds solely if the register still holds the exact value it read a
moment ago. The full action set is: (1) ReadA, in which Terminal A's
instance refreshes its cached view of the shared occupancy register; (2)
CasA, in which Terminal A's instance, provided it still has a bag pending
and its cached read is both fresh (matches the live register) and showed
room under capacity, commits by incrementing the shared register and
consuming one of its pending bags; (3) ReadB, in which Terminal B's instance
refreshes its own cached view of the same shared register; (4) CasB, the
mirror image of CasA for Terminal B's pending bags; and (5) Remove, in which
downstream sorting equipment takes a bag off the shared buffer, decrementing
the shared register and freeing up room that either terminal's instance may
then go on to claim. However the two instances interleave their reads and
compare-and-swaps, the one shared buffer they both depend on must never hold
more bags than its fixed capacity allows.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared sorting buffer's occupancy never exceeds its
fixed capacity, no matter how the two independent terminal instances race to
add bags to it.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag pending at either terminal's instance is
eventually placed into the shared buffer, even though the two instances are
continually competing for the same limited shared capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m1p0t3 ----------------------------
(* A token ring of elevator-bank service stations shares one machine-room  *)
(* door. Only the current token holder may open it. Stations may stall a  *)
(* bounded number of steps (slow, not failed) while holding the token.    *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Station, MaxStall

ASSUME MaxStall \in Nat

Next(p) == IF p = Station THEN 1 ELSE p + 1

VARIABLES token, open, stallBudget, servicing

vars == <<token, open, stallBudget, servicing>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in 1..Station

(* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration for a runway slot allocator. A controller  *)
(* may grant slots only while its own remembered epoch matches the live     *)
(* epoch; silent crashes are modeled by letting reconfiguration occur at    *)
(* any time, whether or not the old controller actually failed.            *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controller, Slot, MaxEpoch

ASSUME MaxEpoch \in Nat

NoEpoch == MaxEpoch + 1

VARIABLES epoch, myEpoch, alloc, pending

vars == <<epoch, myEpoch, alloc, pending>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ myEpoch \in [Controller -> 0..NoEpoch]
    /\ alloc \in [Slot -> SUBSET Controller]
    /\ pending \subseteq Slot

Init ==
    LET c0 == CHOOSE c \in Controller : TRUE IN
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ myEpoch = [c \in Controller |-> IF c = c0 THEN 0 ELSE NoEpoch]
    /\ alloc = [s \in Slot |-> {}]
    /\ pending = {}

Request(s) ==
    /\ s \notin pending
    /\ alloc[s] = {}
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, myEpoch, alloc>>

Reconfigure(c) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ myEpoch' = [myEpoch EXCEPT ![c] = epoch + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, pending>>

Grant(c, s) ==
    /\ myEpoch[c] = epoch
    /\ s \in pending
    /\ alloc[s] = {}
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![s] = @ \cup {c}]
    /\ pending' = pending \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, myEpoch>>

Release(s) ==
    /\ alloc[s] # {}
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, myEpoch, pending>>

RequestAny == \E s \in Slot : Request(s)
ReconfigureAny == \E c \in Controller : Reconfigure(c)
GrantAny == \E c \in Controller, s \in Slot : Grant(c, s)
ReleaseAny == \E s \in Slot : Release(s)
GrantSlot(s) == \E c \in Controller : Grant(c, s)

Next_ == RequestAny \/ ReconfigureAny \/ GrantAny \/ ReleaseAny

(* Per-slot fairness: every individual slot's grant step, not merely some *)
(* slot's grant step, must eventually fire once enabled -- this is what  *)
(* rules out the operator perpetually favoring other slots.              *)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next_]_vars /\ WF_vars(ReconfigureAny) /\ (\A s \in Slot : WF_vars(GrantSlot(s)))

(* A slot's holder set never exceeds one controller: no double allocation. *)
NoDoubleAllocation == \A s \in Slot : Cardinality(alloc[s]) <= 1

(* Every slot that is ever requested is eventually granted. *)
EventualGrant == \A s \in Slot : (s \in pending) ~> (s \notin pending)

nl: A regional air-traffic runway allocator hands out runway slots to arriving flights. Authority to grant a slot is tied to an epoch number: whichever controller was most recently installed remembers that installation's epoch as "my epoch," and only a controller whose remembered epoch still matches the live, current epoch number is allowed to grant slots. A flight first files a request for a slot, which marks that slot as pending. The controller whose remembered epoch matches the live epoch may then grant any pending, currently-free slot to itself; granting places that controller into the slot's holder set and clears the pending mark. A flight that lands and vacates its runway later releases the slot, clearing its holder set back to empty so the slot can be requested again. The four kinds of actions in this system are: a flight filing a request for a slot, the operations desk installing a new controller and advancing the epoch, the controller currently matching the live epoch granting a pending free slot to itself, and a flight releasing a slot it previously held. (* Optimistic-locking settlement for an opening auction. Orders snapshot   *)
(* account versions before transferring; reordered messages can make a    *)
(* snapshot stale, so apply is gated on both versions still matching, and *)
(* a stale order aborts and retries instead of silently mis-transferring. *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, TLC

CONSTANTS A, B, C, o1, o2, Q1, Q2, Bal0

ASSUME Q1 \in Nat /\ Q2 \in Nat /\ Bal0 \in Nat

Account == {A, B, C}
Order == {o1, o2}
Seller == (o1 :> A @@ o2 :> A)
Buyer == (o1 :> B @@ o2 :> C)
Qty == (o1 :> Q1 @@ o2 :> Q2)
InitialBalance == (A :> Bal0 @@ B :> 0 @@ C :> 0)

RECURSIVE SumSet(_, _)
SumSet(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
         IN  f[x] + SumSet(f, S \ {x})

TotalShares == SumSet(InitialBalance, Account)

VARIABLES balance, version, phase, obs

vars == <<balance, version, phase, obs>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ balance \in [Account -> Nat]
    /\ version \in [Account -> Nat]
    /\ phase \in [Order -> {"idle", "reading", "done"}]
    /\ obs \in [Order -> [sv: Nat, bv: Nat]]

Init ==
    /\ balance = InitialBalance
    /\ version = [a \in Account |-> 0]
    /\ phase = [o \in Order |-> "idle"]
    /\ obs = [o \in Order |-> [sv |-> 0, bv |-> 0]]

Begin(o) ==
    /\ phase[o] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "reading"]
    /\ obs' = [obs EXCEPT ![o] = [sv |-> version[Seller[o]], bv |-> version[Buyer[o]]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, version>>

Commit(o) ==
    /\ phase[o] = "reading"
    /\ version[Seller[o]] = obs[o].sv
    /\ version[Buyer[o]] = obs[o].bv
    /\ balance[Seller[o]] >= Qty[o]
    /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![Seller[o]] = @ - Qty[o], ![Buyer[o]] = @ + Qty[o]]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![Seller[o]] = @ + 1, ![Buyer[o]] = @ + 1]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<obs>>

AbortSeller(o) ==
    /\ phase[o] = "reading"
    /\ version[Seller[o]] # obs[o].sv
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, version, obs>>

AbortBuyer(o) ==
    /\ phase[o] = "reading"
    /\ version[Buyer[o]] # obs[o].bv
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, version, obs>>

Next_ == \E o \in Order : Begin(o) \/ Commit(o) \/ AbortSeller(o) \/ AbortBuyer(o)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next_]_vars

(* Optimistic locking must not let reordered snapshots create or destroy  *)
(* shares: the sum across all accounts always equals the starting total. *)
Conservation == SumSet(balance, Account) = TotalShares
=============================================================================

    B = B
    C = C
    o1 = o1
    o2 = o2
    Q1 = 3
    Q2 = 2
    Bal0 = 10
INVARIANT Conservation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl: During the opening auction of a stock exchange, matched orders move shares between settlement accounts. Instead of locking both the seller's and buyer's account for the whole transfer, the settlement engine uses optimistic concurrency: each order first records a snapshot of the current version numbers on the seller and buyer accounts it will touch, without changing any balance yet. Because the exchange's matching messages travel over several parallel links, the record-snapshot and later apply-transfer steps for different orders can be reordered arbitrarily with respect to one another, so a second order might fully settle against one of the same two accounts while the first order's snapshot is still outstanding. When an order later tries to apply its transfer, it only proceeds if the seller's version number and the buyer's version number are both still exactly what it snapshotted; a successful apply moves the fixed share quantity from seller to buyer and bumps both accounts' version numbers. If the messages were reordered such that the seller's account changed underneath it, the order abandons the attempt through a seller-side abort and returns to needing a fresh snapshot; if instead the buyer's account changed underneath it, the order abandons the attempt through a buyer-side abort and likewise returns to needing a fresh snapshot. An order that aborts is free to snapshot again later and retry. The four actions in this system are: an order taking a fresh version snapshot of its seller and buyer accounts, an order applying its transfer once both snapshotted versions still match, an order aborting because the seller account's version moved, and an order aborting because the buyer account's version moved. SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of shares held across all settlement accounts never changes -- no share is ever created or destroyed by a snapshot, apply, or abort.

(* A subway block system advances trains via per-boundary CAS gates.      *)
(* Block capacity can be re-posted at runtime under maintenance mode, but *)
(* never below the fleet size, so it can never permanently trap a train.  *)

CONSTANTS N, TotalTrains, MaxCap

ASSUME N \in Nat /\ TotalTrains \in Nat /\ MaxCap \in Nat /\ MaxCap >= TotalTrains

Blocks == 1..N
Boundaries == 1..(N - 1)

RECURSIVE SumSet(_, _)
SumSet(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
         IN  f[x] + SumSet(f, S \ {x})

VARIABLES occ, cap, gate, capLock

vars == <<occ, cap, gate, capLock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ occ \in [Blocks -> 0..TotalTrains]
    /\ cap \in [Blocks -> TotalTrains..MaxCap]
    /\ gate \in [Boundaries -> {"free", "held"}]
    /\ capLock \in [Blocks -> {"normal", "maintenance"}]

Init ==
    /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> IF b = 1 THEN TotalTrains ELSE 0]
    /\ cap = [b \in Blocks |-> MaxCap]
    /\ gate = [i \in Boundaries |-> "free"]
    /\ capLock = [b \in Blocks |-> "normal"]

ToggleMaintenance(b) ==
    /\ capLock' = [capLock EXCEPT ![b] = IF @ = "normal" THEN "maintenance" ELSE "normal"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, cap, gate>>

SetCapacity(b) ==
    /\ capLock[b] = "maintenance"
    /\ \E newCap \in TotalTrains..MaxCap :
        cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![b] = newCap]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, gate, capLock>>

AcquireGate(i) ==
    /\ gate[i] = "free"
    /\ gate' = [gate EXCEPT ![i] = "held"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, cap, capLock>>

MoveTrain(i) ==
    /\ gate[i] = "held"
    /\ occ[i] > 0
    /\ occ[i + 1] < cap[i + 1]
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1, ![i + 1] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, gate, capLock>>

ReleaseGate(i) ==
    /\ gate[i] = "held"
    /\ gate' = [gate EXCEPT ![i] = "free"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, cap, capLock>>

Next_ ==
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : ToggleMaintenance(b) \/ SetCapacity(b)
    \/ \E i \in Boundaries : AcquireGate(i) \/ MoveTrain(i) \/ ReleaseGate(i)

BoundaryFair(i) == SF_vars(AcquireGate(i)) /\ SF_vars(MoveTrain(i)) /\ SF_vars(ReleaseGate(i))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next_]_vars /\ (\A i \in Boundaries : BoundaryFair(i))

(* Conservation: the CAS-gated shuffle never creates or destroys a train. *)
Conservation == SumSet(occ, Blocks) = TotalTrains

(* Every train eventually reaches the terminal block. *)
EventualArrival == <>(occ[N] = TotalTrains)

nl: A subway line is divided into a fixed row of signalling blocks numbered from the platform to the far terminus, and the signalling computer must never lose or duplicate a train as it advances trains block by block toward the terminus. Between each pair of adjacent blocks sits a single compare-and-swap gate register that starts "free"; a train may only cross from one block into the next after that boundary's gate has been compare-and-swapped from "free" to "held" in its favor, and the crossing itself does not complete until the gate is later compare-and-swapped back from "held" to "free". While a gate is held, the train physically moves out of the block behind it and into the block ahead of it, provided the block ahead still has room under its currently posted capacity. Maintenance crews can put an individual block into a maintenance mode and, only while it is in that mode, re-post a new capacity figure for that block, and they can take the block back out of maintenance mode again at any time -- so a block's rated capacity can rise or fall at runtime, though never below the size of the whole in-service fleet, since the signalling system will not accept a posted ceiling lower than every train it is currently responsible for. The five actions in this system are: toggling a block's maintenance mode on or off, posting a new capacity figure for a block that is currently in maintenance mode, compare-and-swapping a boundary's gate from free to held, moving a train out of the block behind a held gate and into the block ahead of it, and compare-and-swapping a boundary's gate back from held to free. SAFETY PROPERTY: the total count of trains summed across every block never changes -- the signalling computer neither creates nor destroys a train as it shuffles the fleet forward. LIVENESS PROPERTY: every train in the fleet eventually reaches the terminal block at the end of the line.

(* A term-numbered CAS register gates enrollment commits. Validating stamps *)
(* an advisor's credential with the live term; committing only checks that *)
(* the credential is still held, so correctness depends on the registrar's *)
(* term rollover wiping every held credential at once, preventing a stale  *)
(* or crashed advisor's leftover credential from ever being spent later.   *)
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Advisor, MaxTerm, MaxLog

ASSUME MaxTerm \in Nat /\ MaxLog \in Nat

VARIABLES termReg, ticket, validated, crashed, log

vars == <<termReg, ticket, validated, crashed, log>>

LogEntry == [actor: Advisor, ticketTerm: 0..MaxTerm, commitTerm: 0..MaxTerm]

TypeOK ==
    /\ termReg \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ ticket \in [Advisor -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ validated \subseteq Advisor
    /\ crashed \subseteq Advisor
    /\ log \in Seq(LogEntry)

Init ==
    /\ termReg = 0
    /\ ticket = [a \in Advisor |-> 0]
    /\ validated = {}
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ log = <<>>

Validate(a) ==
    /\ a \notin crashed
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![a] = termReg]
    /\ validated' = validated \cup {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<termReg, crashed, log>>

AdvanceTerm ==
    /\ termReg < MaxTerm
    /\ termReg' = termReg + 1
    /\ validated' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ticket, crashed, log>>

Commit(a) ==
    /\ a \in validated
    /\ a \notin crashed
    /\ Len(log) < MaxLog
    /\ log' = Append(log, [actor |-> a, ticketTerm |-> ticket[a], commitTerm |-> termReg])
    /\ validated' = validated \ {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<termReg, ticket, crashed>>

Crash(a) ==
    /\ a \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<termReg, ticket, validated, log>>

Next_ == (\E a \in Advisor : Validate(a) \/ Commit(a) \/ Crash(a)) \/ AdvanceTerm

Spec == Init /\ [][Next_]_vars

(* No advisor ever commits with a term-stale or already-invalid credential: *)
(* the term recorded on validation must match the term live at commit time. *)

    a2 = a2

nl: A university's course-registration system gates every seat-committing action behind a single compare-and-swap term register that names the currently open registration term. An academic advisor who wants to commit a student's enrollment must first validate against the register, which stamps the advisor with whatever term number is live at that instant and marks the advisor as holding a validated credential. ---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m7p6t3 ----------------------------
(* Per-bay CAS holder registers plus generation counters for a crane yard. *)
(* A crane's lease records the generation it observed at acquire time; a   *)
(* forced dispatcher reassignment bumps the generation and invalidates    *)
(* the lease, so a slow (never-failed) crane can only finish while its    *)
(* lease is still marked valid -- otherwise its finish would be stale.    *)

ASSUME NoCrane \notin Crane
ASSUME NoBay \notin Bay

VARIABLES gen, holder, lease, stall, log

vars == <<gen, holder, lease, stall, log>>

LeaseType == [bay: Bay \cup {NoBay}, obsGen: 0..MaxGen, valid: BOOLEAN]
LogEntry == [present: BOOLEAN, crane: Crane, obsGen: 0..MaxGen, curGen: 0..MaxGen]

TypeOK ==
    /\ gen \in [Bay -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ holder \in [Bay -> Crane \cup {NoCrane}]
    /\ lease \in [Crane -> LeaseType]
    /\ stall \in [Crane -> 0..MaxStall]
    /\ log \in LogEntry

Init ==
    /\ gen = [b \in Bay |-> 0]
    /\ holder = [b \in Bay |-> NoCrane]
    /\ lease = [c \in Crane |-> [bay |-> NoBay, obsGen |-> 0, valid |-> FALSE]]
    /\ stall = [c \in Crane |-> 0]
    /\ log = [present |-> FALSE, crane |-> CHOOSE c \in Crane : TRUE, obsGen |-> 0, curGen |-> 0]

Acquire(c, b) ==
    /\ holder[b] = NoCrane
    /\ ~lease[c].valid
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = c]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![c] = [bay |-> b, obsGen |-> gen[b], valid |-> TRUE]]
    /\ stall' = [stall EXCEPT ![c] = MaxStall]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, log>>

StallStep(c) ==
    /\ lease[c].valid
    /\ stall[c] > 0
    /\ stall' = [stall EXCEPT ![c] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, holder, lease, log>>

Reassign(b) ==
    /\ holder[b] # NoCrane
    /\ gen[b] < MaxGen
    /\ LET c == holder[b] IN
        /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = NoCrane]
        /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
        /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![c].valid = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stall, log>>

Commit(c) ==
    /\ lease[c].valid
    /\ LET b == lease[c].bay IN
        /\ log' = [present |-> TRUE, crane |-> c, obsGen |-> lease[c].obsGen, curGen |-> gen[b]]
        /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = IF holder[b] = c THEN NoCrane ELSE holder[b]]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![c].valid = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, stall>>

Next_ ==
    \/ \E c \in Crane, b \in Bay : Acquire(c, b)
    \/ \E c \in Crane : StallStep(c) \/ Commit(c)
    \/ \E b \in Bay : Reassign(b)

CommitFair(c) == WF_vars(Commit(c))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next_]_vars /\ (\A c \in Crane : CommitFair(c))

(* A finish's recorded generation must match the bay's live generation at *)
(* that same instant -- no crane ever finishes on a reassigned-away lease. *)
NoStaleFinish == log.present => (log.obsGen = log.curGen)

    NoBay = NoBay
    MaxGen = 1
    MaxStall = 1

nl: A container-ship crane yard tracks, for every crane bay, a compare-and-swap holder register plus a generation counter that the yard dispatcher bumps whenever it forcibly reassigns that bay. A crane wanting to work a bay compare-and-swaps the bay's holder register from free to itself and, in that same step, privately records which bay it took and what generation the bay was at when it took it -- this recorded pair is its lease. A crane is never simply failed; it can only be slow, and while it holds a lease it may take any number of bounded stalling steps before finishing, never losing the lease just by being unhurried. Because slow cranes tie up valuable bays, the dispatcher may at any moment forcibly reassign a bay that currently has a holder: doing so frees the holder register, bumps that bay's generation counter, and marks the former holder's lease as no longer valid. A crane finishes its work by spending its lease -- provided the lease is still marked valid -- overwriting a single shared finish record with both the generation it originally recorded and the bay's actual live generation at that same instant, then invalidating its own lease and, if it is still genuinely the bay's holder, freeing the holder register too. ASSUME NoPatron \notin Patron
