---- MODULE W4Od1m0p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Runway slot allocation by optimistic locking with retry: a flight reads a
\* slot's current version, then sends a propose message carrying that
\* version over an asynchronous network. The network is modelled as a SET
\* of in-flight messages rather than a queue, so it may deliver -- or the
\* tower may garbage-collect -- proposals in any order, out of send order.
\* A proposal only commits if its carried version still matches the slot's
\* live version at processing time, which is what keeps a stale, reordered
\* proposal from ever double-allocating a slot.

CONSTANTS Flights, Slots, MaxVersion

ASSUME MaxVersion \in Nat

VARIABLES slotOwner, slotVersion, network, allocated

vars == <<slotOwner, slotVersion, network, allocated>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ slotOwner \in [Slots -> Flights \cup {"free"}]
  /\ slotVersion \in [Slots -> 0..MaxVersion]
  /\ network \subseteq (Flights \X Slots \X (0..MaxVersion))
  /\ allocated \in [Flights -> Slots \cup {"none"}]

Init ==
  /\ slotOwner = [s \in Slots |-> "free"]
  /\ slotVersion = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ network = {}
  /\ allocated = [f \in Flights |-> "none"]

\* Read the slot's current version and send a propose message carrying it.
\* Also how a flight retries after a failed attempt: it simply proposes
\* again, reading whatever the version happens to be now.
Propose(f, s) ==
  /\ allocated[f] = "none"
  /\ slotVersion[s] < MaxVersion
  /\ network' = network \cup {<<f, s, slotVersion[s]>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotVersion, allocated>>

\* The tower processes some pending proposal -- any one of them, chosen
\* independently of send order, which is how reordering shows up here. It
\* commits only if the carried version still matches the slot's live
\* version and the slot is still free; otherwise the optimistic lock has
\* failed and the message is simply consumed with no effect.
ProcessPropose(f, s, v) ==
  /\ <<f, s, v>> \in network
  /\ network' = network \ {<<f, s, v>>}
  /\ IF v = slotVersion[s] /\ slotOwner[s] = "free" /\ allocated[f] = "none"
     THEN /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = f]
          /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
          /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![f] = s]
     ELSE UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotVersion, allocated>>

\* The tower garbage-collects a proposal it can already tell is stale
\* (its carried version trails the slot's live version) without bothering
\* to run it through the commit check.
DropStale(f, s, v) ==
  /\ <<f, s, v>> \in network
  /\ v < slotVersion[s]
  /\ network' = network \ {<<f, s, v>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotVersion, allocated>>

\* A flight cancels and gives its runway slot back, freeing it for others.
Release(f) ==
  /\ allocated[f] # "none"
  /\ LET s == allocated[f] IN
       /\ slotVersion[s] < MaxVersion
       /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = "free"]
       /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![f] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED network

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Flights, s \in Slots : Propose(f, s)
  \/ \E f \in Flights, s \in Slots, v \in 0..MaxVersion : ProcessPropose(f, s, v)
  \/ \E f \in Flights, s \in Slots, v \in 0..MaxVersion : DropStale(f, s, v)
  \/ \E f \in Flights : Release(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: no double allocation of the same runway slot. Whatever a flight
\* records as its held slot always agrees with the slot's own record of its
\* owner, and no two distinct flights ever record the same held slot.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  /\ \A f \in Flights : allocated[f] # "none" => slotOwner[allocated[f]] = f
  /\ \A f1, f2 \in Flights :
       (allocated[f1] # "none" /\ allocated[f1] = allocated[f2]) => f1 = f2

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Flights = {f1, f2, f3}
  Slots = {s1, s2}
  MaxVersion = 3
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator hands out a small set of scheduled runway
slots to flights using optimistic locking with retry. A flight that wants a
slot reads that slot's current version number and sends a propose message
carrying the version it saw off into the tower's messaging network. That
network is asynchronous: it holds proposals as an unordered pool of
in-flight messages rather than a first-in-first-out queue, so the tower can
end up processing them in any order -- not necessarily the order in which
they were sent. When the tower processes a proposal, it commits the
allocation only if the version the message carries still matches the slot's
live version and the slot is still free; if either has changed since the
flight read it, the optimistic lock has failed and the proposal is simply
consumed with no effect, leaving the flight to retry by proposing again
against whatever version is now current. The tower may also proactively
garbage-collect a proposal it can already tell is stale -- its carried
version trailing the slot's current version -- without running it through
the commit check at all. A flight holding a slot may also cancel, releasing
it back to "free" and bumping its version so that any old, now-obsolete
proposals for it are guaranteed to fail their version check.

The full action set is: Propose (a flight reads a slot's current version and
sends a proposal carrying it, also how a flight retries after a failed
attempt), ProcessPropose (the tower processes some pending proposal, in
whatever order it happens to pick, committing it if the carried version
still matches and the slot is free, otherwise discarding it as a failed
optimistic lock), DropStale (the tower discards a proposal it can already
tell is stale without running the commit check), and Release (a flight
holding a slot cancels and frees it, advancing its version).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the same runway slot is never double-allocated -- every
flight's record of the slot it holds always agrees with that slot's own
record of its owner, and no two distinct flights ever end up recording the
same held slot.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m7p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* An airport baggage router where two independently-operated sorter
\* instances ("A" and "B", one per terminal) share a single bounded holding
\* buffer between the belts and the loading bay. Admission and removal are
\* both governed by a compare-and-swap register (poolCount): an instance
\* reads the register, then attempts to swap it, retrying from the read if
\* the other instance's own CAS beat it to the register in between. The
\* invariant guards that the shared buffer's bound is never exceeded even
\* though both instances contend for the very same register.

CONSTANTS BagsA, BagsB, Capacity

ASSUME Capacity \in Nat

Bags == BagsA \cup BagsB
Instances == {"A", "B"}
OwnerOf(b) == IF b \in BagsA THEN "A" ELSE "B"
MaxCount == Cardinality(Bags)

VARIABLES bagState, poolCount, pendingBag, pendingSnapshot

vars == <<bagState, poolCount, pendingBag, pendingSnapshot>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ bagState \in [Bags -> {"queued", "inpool", "delivered"}]
  /\ poolCount \in 0..MaxCount
  /\ pendingBag \in [Instances -> Bags \cup {"none"}]
  /\ pendingSnapshot \in [Instances -> 0..MaxCount]

Init ==
  /\ bagState = [b \in Bags |-> "queued"]
  /\ poolCount = 0
  /\ pendingBag = [i \in Instances |-> "none"]
  /\ pendingSnapshot = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

\* Read phase for admitting a bag into the shared buffer: snapshot the
\* register before attempting the swap.
StartInsert(i, b) ==
  /\ OwnerOf(b) = i
  /\ bagState[b] = "queued"
  /\ pendingBag[i] = "none"
  /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![i] = b]
  /\ pendingSnapshot' = [pendingSnapshot EXCEPT ![i] = poolCount]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bagState, poolCount>>

\* Swap phase: succeeds only if the register still reads what this instance
\* last saw AND there is still room under the shared cap; otherwise this is
\* a failed compare-and-swap and the instance must go back and re-read.
CasInsert(i) ==
  /\ pendingBag[i] # "none"
  /\ bagState[pendingBag[i]] = "queued"
  /\ LET b == pendingBag[i] IN
       IF poolCount = pendingSnapshot[i] /\ poolCount < Capacity
       THEN /\ poolCount' = poolCount + 1
            /\ bagState' = [bagState EXCEPT ![b] = "inpool"]
            /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![i] = "none"]
            /\ UNCHANGED pendingSnapshot
       ELSE /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![i] = "none"]
            /\ UNCHANGED <<poolCount, bagState, pendingSnapshot>>

\* Read phase for handing a bag out of the shared buffer to its terminal.
StartRemove(i, b) ==
  /\ OwnerOf(b) = i
  /\ bagState[b] = "inpool"
  /\ pendingBag[i] = "none"
  /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![i] = b]
  /\ pendingSnapshot' = [pendingSnapshot EXCEPT ![i] = poolCount]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bagState, poolCount>>

\* Swap phase for removal: same compare-and-swap discipline, freeing one
\* unit of shared capacity on success.
CasRemove(i) ==
  /\ pendingBag[i] # "none"
  /\ bagState[pendingBag[i]] = "inpool"
  /\ LET b == pendingBag[i] IN
       IF poolCount = pendingSnapshot[i]
       THEN /\ poolCount' = poolCount - 1
            /\ bagState' = [bagState EXCEPT ![b] = "delivered"]
            /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![i] = "none"]
            /\ UNCHANGED pendingSnapshot
       ELSE /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![i] = "none"]
            /\ UNCHANGED <<poolCount, bagState, pendingSnapshot>>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Bags : StartInsert(i, b)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : CasInsert(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Bags : StartRemove(i, b)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : CasRemove(i)

Fairness ==
  \A i \in Instances :
    /\ SF_vars(\E b \in Bags : StartInsert(i, b))
    /\ SF_vars(CasInsert(i))
    /\ SF_vars(\E b \in Bags : StartRemove(i, b))
    /\ SF_vars(CasRemove(i))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: the shared buffer's bound is never exceeded by either instance's
\* traffic, even though both contend for the same compare-and-swap register.
BoundedCapacity == poolCount <= Capacity

\* LIVENESS: every bag either instance queues eventually gets all the way
\* through the shared buffer and out, regardless of how the two instances'
\* compare-and-swap attempts interleave and race on the shared register.
BagDelivered == \A b \in Bags : (bagState[b] = "queued") ~> (bagState[b] = "delivered")

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  BagsA = {a1, a2}
  BagsB = {b1, b2}
  Capacity = 2
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
PROPERTY BagDelivered
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airport runs two independently operated baggage-sorter instances, one
serving Terminal A's belts and one serving Terminal B's, but both funnel
bags through a single shared holding buffer between the sorters and the
loading bay -- the two instances are otherwise completely independent, they
just happen to share this one pool of buffer capacity. Admission to and
removal from the shared buffer are both governed by a single compare-and-swap
register that holds the current occupancy count. To admit one of its own
bags, an instance first reads the register's current value, then attempts to
swap it to one higher; the swap only succeeds if the register still holds
the value the instance last read and there is still room under the shared
cap, otherwise the compare-and-swap has failed (the other instance's own
traffic changed the register in between) and the instance must go back and
re-read before trying again. Removing a bag from the buffer once it reaches
its own terminal works the same way in reverse: read the register, then
attempt to swap it one lower, retrying on failure. Because both instances
hit the very same register, an admission by one and a removal by the other
can interleave in any order, and the compare-and-swap discipline is what
keeps the shared buffer's bound safe despite that contention.

The full action set is: StartInsert (an instance snapshots the register
before trying to admit one of its own queued bags), CasInsert (the instance
attempts the compare-and-swap that admits the bag, succeeding only if the
register still matches its snapshot and there is room, otherwise failing and
forcing a retry), StartRemove (an instance snapshots the register before
trying to hand off one of its own buffered bags), and CasRemove (the
instance attempts the compare-and-swap that removes the bag, succeeding only
if the register still matches its snapshot).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared buffer's bound is never exceeded, no matter how
the two instances' compare-and-swap attempts on the one shared register
interleave.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bag either instance queues into the shared buffer
is eventually delivered all the way through and out, regardless of how the
two instances' compare-and-swap retries race against each other.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m1p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* An elevator bank in a skyscraper shares one express shaft segment (a
\* single-track pass-through used by every car to cross between low- and
\* high-rise zones) that only one car may occupy at a time. A token
\* circulates around the bank in a fixed ring order; only the car currently
\* holding the token may enter the shared segment. The invariant guards
\* mutual exclusion of that segment by tying occupancy directly to token
\* possession, not by counting occupants.

CONSTANTS NumCars

ASSUME NumCars \in Nat /\ NumCars >= 2

Cars == 1..NumCars
Succ(c) == IF c = NumCars THEN 1 ELSE c + 1

VARIABLES tokenHolder, inCritical, slow, dwelled

vars == <<tokenHolder, inCritical, slow, dwelled>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ tokenHolder \in Cars
  /\ inCritical \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ slow \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ dwelled \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ tokenHolder = 1
  /\ inCritical = [c \in Cars |-> FALSE]
  /\ slow = [c \in Cars |-> FALSE]
  /\ dwelled = [c \in Cars |-> FALSE]

\* Only the token holder may enter, and a car flagged slow must first have
\* dwelled once this turn -- extra door-open time before it may cross.
EnterCritical(c) ==
  /\ tokenHolder = c
  /\ ~inCritical[c]
  /\ (~slow[c] \/ dwelled[c])
  /\ inCritical' = [inCritical EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, slow, dwelled>>

ExitCritical(c) ==
  /\ inCritical[c]
  /\ inCritical' = [inCritical EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, slow, dwelled>>

\* Twist: a slow car is never failed or skipped, it simply must take one
\* extra dwell step before it is allowed to cross the shared segment.
Dwell(c) ==
  /\ tokenHolder = c
  /\ slow[c]
  /\ ~inCritical[c]
  /\ ~dwelled[c]
  /\ dwelled' = [dwelled EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, inCritical, slow>>

\* The token passes on only once its holder has left the shared segment.
PassToken(c) ==
  /\ tokenHolder = c
  /\ ~inCritical[c]
  /\ tokenHolder' = Succ(c)
  /\ dwelled' = [dwelled EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inCritical, slow>>

\* Dispatch may flag or clear a car as running slow only while it does not
\* hold the token, so speed cannot change mid-turn.
SetSlow(c) ==
  /\ tokenHolder # c
  /\ ~slow[c]
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, inCritical, dwelled>>

ClearSlow(c) ==
  /\ tokenHolder # c
  /\ slow[c]
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, inCritical, dwelled>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars : EnterCritical(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : ExitCritical(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Dwell(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : PassToken(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : SetSlow(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : ClearSlow(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: mutual exclusion of the shared shaft segment, guarded via the
\* mechanism itself -- a car may only be inside the segment while it is the
\* current token holder, so at most one car can ever be inside at once.
TokenGatesAccess == \A c \in Cars : inCritical[c] => tokenHolder = c

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  NumCars = 4
INVARIANT TokenGatesAccess
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank has several cars sharing one express shaft
segment -- a single-track pass-through section used by every car to cross
between the low-rise and high-rise zones, wide enough for only one car at a
time. Exclusive access to that shared segment is granted by a token that
circulates around the bank of cars in a fixed ring order: car 1 passes it to
car 2, and so on back around to car 1. Only the car currently holding the
token may enter the shared segment, and it must leave the segment again
before it is allowed to pass the token on to the next car in the ring, so
the token and occupancy of the segment stay tied together. Building
dispatch can flag any car that is not currently holding the token as
"running slow" (for instance its doors are sticking) without ever failing
it or pulling it out of the ring -- a slow car simply must take one extra
dwell step, holding position with its doors open a beat longer, before it is
allowed to actually cross into the shared segment on its turn; an ordinary
car skips that step. Dispatch can also clear the slow flag once the car is
running normally again, again only while it does not hold the token.

The full action set is: EnterCritical (the token holder enters the shared
shaft segment, provided it has dwelled if it is flagged slow), ExitCritical
(the car currently in the segment leaves it), Dwell (a slow car holding the
token takes its required extra step before it may enter), PassToken (the
token holder, having left the segment, passes the token to the next car in
the ring), SetSlow (dispatch flags a car that does not hold the token as
running slow), and ClearSlow (dispatch clears the slow flag from a car that
does not hold the token).

SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one car is ever inside the shared shaft segment at
a time, because a car may only be inside it while it is the current token
holder.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m9p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* An air-traffic runway allocator reconfigured by epoch number. A
\* controller proposes to allocate a free slot to a flight, stamping the
\* proposal with the epoch it currently believes is live, then the system
\* processes that proposal later (perhaps much later). The proposal only
\* commits if its stamped epoch still matches the live epoch -- this is
\* what fences off a controller that crashed silently mid-epoch: once
\* reconfiguration bumps the epoch, that controller's outstanding proposals
\* can never commit, so its silence can never cause a slot to be handed to
\* two different flights.

CONSTANTS Controllers, Flights, Slots, MaxEpoch

ASSUME MaxEpoch \in Nat

VARIABLES epoch, crashed, slotOwner, holds, proposals

vars == <<epoch, crashed, slotOwner, holds, proposals>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ crashed \subseteq Controllers
  /\ slotOwner \in [Slots -> Flights \cup {"free"}]
  /\ holds \in [Flights -> Slots \cup {"none"}]
  /\ proposals \subseteq (Controllers \X Slots \X Flights \X (0..MaxEpoch))

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ slotOwner = [s \in Slots |-> "free"]
  /\ holds = [f \in Flights |-> "none"]
  /\ proposals = {}

\* A live controller proposes allocating a free slot to a flight, stamping
\* the proposal with the epoch it currently believes is live.
Propose(c, s, f) ==
  /\ c \notin crashed
  /\ slotOwner[s] = "free"
  /\ holds[f] = "none"
  /\ <<c, s, f, epoch>> \notin proposals
  /\ proposals' = proposals \cup {<<c, s, f, epoch>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed, slotOwner, holds>>

\* The system processes some pending proposal, in whatever order. It
\* commits only if the proposal's stamped epoch still matches the live
\* epoch and the slot is still free; otherwise it is fenced off (stale, or
\* superseded) and simply discarded.
ProcessPropose(c, s, f, e) ==
  /\ <<c, s, f, e>> \in proposals
  /\ proposals' = proposals \ {<<c, s, f, e>>}
  /\ IF e = epoch /\ slotOwner[s] = "free" /\ holds[f] = "none"
     THEN /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = f]
          /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![f] = s]
     ELSE UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, holds>>
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed>>

\* A controller crashes silently: no announcement, it simply never proposes
\* again. Its already-sent proposals stay in flight until processed.
CrashSilently(c) ==
  /\ c \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, slotOwner, holds, proposals>>

\* Reconfiguration: once some controller is known to have crashed, the
\* system may bump the epoch, fencing off every proposal stamped with the
\* old epoch or earlier.
Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ \E c \in Controllers : c \in crashed
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, slotOwner, holds, proposals>>

\* A flight cancels, freeing its slot back up.
Release(f) ==
  /\ holds[f] # "none"
  /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![holds[f]] = "free"]
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![f] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed, proposals>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, s \in Slots, f \in Flights : Propose(c, s, f)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, s \in Slots, f \in Flights, e \in 0..MaxEpoch :
       ProcessPropose(c, s, f, e)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : CrashSilently(c)
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E f \in Flights : Release(f)

Fairness ==
  \A c \in Controllers, s \in Slots, f \in Flights, e \in 0..MaxEpoch :
    WF_vars(ProcessPropose(c, s, f, e))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: no double allocation of the same runway slot. What a flight
\* records as its held slot always agrees with that slot's own record of
\* its owner, and no two distinct flights ever record the same held slot.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  /\ \A f \in Flights : holds[f] # "none" => slotOwner[holds[f]] = f
  /\ \A f1, f2 \in Flights :
       (holds[f1] # "none" /\ holds[f1] = holds[f2]) => f1 = f2

\* LIVENESS: every proposal, whether it ends up committing or getting
\* fenced off by a later reconfiguration, is eventually resolved -- a
\* silently crashed controller's abandoned proposals never hang forever.
ProposalsResolve ==
  \A c \in Controllers, s \in Slots, f \in Flights, e \in 0..MaxEpoch :
    (<<c, s, f, e>> \in proposals) ~> (<<c, s, f, e>> \notin proposals)

====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator hands its authority off between controllers
using epoch-numbered reconfiguration. Whichever controller is active
proposes to allocate a free runway slot to a flight by stamping its proposal
with the epoch number it currently believes is live and dropping it into a
pending pool; the system processes pending proposals later, in whatever
order, and a proposal only commits -- setting that flight as the slot's
owner -- if its stamped epoch still matches the live epoch and the slot is
still actually free. One controller can crash silently at any time: it
simply stops proposing anything further, with no announcement to anyone,
and any proposals it already sent stay sitting in the pending pool exactly
as before. Once a controller is known to have crashed, the system may bump
the global epoch number, which is the reconfiguration step -- and the
moment that happens, every proposal still carrying the old epoch number (or
older) can never commit, because its stamped epoch no longer matches the
live one, so the crashed controller's silence can never let a stale
proposal slip through and hand a slot to two different flights. A flight
holding a slot may also cancel, releasing it back to free.

The full action set is: Propose (a live controller proposes allocating a
free slot to a flight, stamped with the epoch it currently believes is
live), ProcessPropose (the system processes some pending proposal, in
whatever order, committing it if the stamped epoch still matches the live
epoch and the slot is still free, otherwise discarding it as fenced off),
CrashSilently (a controller crashes without announcement and never proposes
again), Reconfigure (once some controller is known to have crashed, the
system bumps the epoch, fencing off every proposal from the old epoch or
earlier), and Release (a flight holding a slot cancels and frees it).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the same runway slot is never double-allocated -- every
flight's record of the slot it holds always agrees with that slot's own
record of its owner, and no two distinct flights ever end up recording the
same held slot.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every proposal is eventually resolved, either committed
or discarded as fenced off, so a silently crashed controller's abandoned
proposals never hang in the pending pool forever.

---- MODULE W4Od15m0p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* A stock exchange's opening auction matches a fixed pool of individual
\* share units against buyers using optimistic locking with retry: a buyer
\* snapshots a share's book version, sends a claim proposal over an
\* asynchronous network (a SET of in-flight messages, not a queue, so
\* delivery can be reordered relative to send order), and the claim commits
\* only if the version still matches at processing time. The invariant
\* guards conservation: every share the exchange has actually executed a
\* match for is reflected in exactly one buyer's holdings ledger, and
\* nothing in that ledger exists without a genuine matched share behind it
\* -- shares are neither fabricated nor lost as claims race and retry.

CONSTANTS Shares, Buyers, MaxVersion

ASSUME MaxVersion \in Nat

VARIABLES shareState, shareBuyer, bookVersion, network, heldByBuyer

vars == <<shareState, shareBuyer, bookVersion, network, heldByBuyer>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ shareState \in [Shares -> {"forsale", "reserved", "matched"}]
  /\ shareBuyer \in [Shares -> Buyers \cup {"none"}]
  /\ bookVersion \in [Shares -> 0..MaxVersion]
  /\ network \subseteq (Buyers \X Shares \X (0..MaxVersion))
  /\ heldByBuyer \in [Buyers -> SUBSET Shares]

Init ==
  /\ shareState = [sh \in Shares |-> "forsale"]
  /\ shareBuyer = [sh \in Shares |-> "none"]
  /\ bookVersion = [sh \in Shares |-> 0]
  /\ network = {}
  /\ heldByBuyer = [b \in Buyers |-> {}]

\* A buyer reads a share's current book version and sends a claim proposal
\* carrying it -- this is also how a buyer retries after a failed attempt.
ProposeClaim(b, sh) ==
  /\ shareState[sh] = "forsale"
  /\ bookVersion[sh] < MaxVersion
  /\ network' = network \cup {<<b, sh, bookVersion[sh]>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shareState, shareBuyer, bookVersion, heldByBuyer>>

\* The exchange processes some pending claim -- any one of them, independent
\* of send order, which is how reordering shows up here. It commits only if
\* the carried version still matches the share's live book version and the
\* share is still for sale; otherwise the optimistic lock has failed and
\* the proposal is simply discarded.
ProcessClaim(b, sh, v) ==
  /\ <<b, sh, v>> \in network
  /\ network' = network \ {<<b, sh, v>>}
  /\ IF v = bookVersion[sh] /\ shareState[sh] = "forsale"
     THEN /\ shareState' = [shareState EXCEPT ![sh] = "reserved"]
          /\ shareBuyer' = [shareBuyer EXCEPT ![sh] = b]
          /\ bookVersion' = [bookVersion EXCEPT ![sh] = @ + 1]
     ELSE UNCHANGED <<shareState, shareBuyer, bookVersion>>
  /\ UNCHANGED heldByBuyer

\* The exchange finalizes a reserved claim into an executed match, crediting
\* the share to the buyer's holdings ledger.
ConfirmMatch(sh) ==
  /\ shareState[sh] = "reserved"
  /\ bookVersion[sh] < MaxVersion
  /\ shareState' = [shareState EXCEPT ![sh] = "matched"]
  /\ bookVersion' = [bookVersion EXCEPT ![sh] = @ + 1]
  /\ heldByBuyer' = [heldByBuyer EXCEPT ![shareBuyer[sh]] = @ \cup {sh}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shareBuyer, network>>

\* A reservation lapses (the buyer withdraws, or it times out): the share
\* goes back on the book, unmatched and unowned -- it is never destroyed,
\* only returned to circulation.
CancelReservation(sh) ==
  /\ shareState[sh] = "reserved"
  /\ bookVersion[sh] < MaxVersion
  /\ shareState' = [shareState EXCEPT ![sh] = "forsale"]
  /\ shareBuyer' = [shareBuyer EXCEPT ![sh] = "none"]
  /\ bookVersion' = [bookVersion EXCEPT ![sh] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<heldByBuyer, network>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Buyers, sh \in Shares : ProposeClaim(b, sh)
  \/ \E b \in Buyers, sh \in Shares, v \in 0..MaxVersion : ProcessClaim(b, sh, v)
  \/ \E sh \in Shares : ConfirmMatch(sh)
  \/ \E sh \in Shares : CancelReservation(sh)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: conservation of shares. Every share the exchange has actually
\* matched is reflected in exactly one buyer's holdings ledger under its
\* true buyer, and the ledger holds nothing that isn't a genuinely matched
\* share -- no share is ever fabricated into or lost from a buyer's tally.
ShareConservation ==
  /\ \A sh \in Shares :
       shareState[sh] = "matched" => sh \in heldByBuyer[shareBuyer[sh]]
  /\ \A b \in Buyers :
       \A sh \in heldByBuyer[b] : shareState[sh] = "matched" /\ shareBuyer[sh] = b

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Shares = {sh1, sh2, sh3}
  Buyers = {b1, b2}
  MaxVersion = 3
INVARIANT ShareConservation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction over a small, fixed pool of
individual share units waiting to be matched against buyers, using
optimistic locking with retry. To claim a share, a buyer reads that share's
current book version and sends a claim proposal carrying the version it saw
into the exchange's matching network. That network is asynchronous: it
holds claim proposals as an unordered pool of in-flight messages rather
than a first-in-first-out queue, so the exchange can end up processing them
in any order, not necessarily the order in which they were sent. When the
exchange processes a claim proposal, it reserves the share for that buyer
only if the version the proposal carries still matches the share's live
book version and the share is still on the book for sale; if either has
changed, the optimistic lock has failed and the proposal is simply
discarded, leaving the buyer to retry by proposing again against whatever
version is now current. A reserved share is later either finalized by the
exchange into an executed match -- crediting the share to that buyer's
holdings ledger -- or its reservation lapses and the share goes back onto
the book for sale, unowned, exactly as it was before, never destroyed and
never duplicated.

The full action set is: ProposeClaim (a buyer reads a share's current book
version and sends a claim proposal carrying it, also how a buyer retries
after a failed attempt), ProcessClaim (the exchange processes some pending
claim, in whatever order it happens to pick, reserving the share for that
buyer if the carried version still matches and the share is still for sale,
otherwise discarding it as a failed optimistic lock), ConfirmMatch (the
exchange finalizes a reserved share into an executed match and credits it
to the buyer's holdings ledger), and CancelReservation (a reserved share's
claim lapses and it returns to the book for sale, unowned).

SAFETY PROPERTY: shares are conserved -- every share the exchange has
actually matched is reflected in exactly one buyer's holdings ledger under
its true buyer, and that ledger never holds a share that isn't genuinely
matched to it, so no share is ever fabricated into or lost from the
exchange's books.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m7p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* A subway signalling block system tracks spare block capacity in a single
\* shared compare-and-swap register (freeSlots). A train wanting to enter
\* or leave the occupied block set snapshots the register, then attempts an
\* atomic swap that only succeeds if the register still holds what it last
\* saw, retrying from a fresh snapshot on failure. Maintenance can also
\* open or retire block segments at runtime, growing or shrinking the
\* system's total capacity. The invariant guards conservation: the register
\* never reports more spare capacity than the line's live total actually
\* grants, no matter how capacity or occupancy moves around it.

CONSTANTS Trains, MaxTotalCapacity, InitialCapacity

ASSUME /\ MaxTotalCapacity \in Nat
       /\ InitialCapacity \in 0..MaxTotalCapacity

VARIABLES totalCapacity, freeSlots, trainSnapshot, trainPending, occupied

vars == <<totalCapacity, freeSlots, trainSnapshot, trainPending, occupied>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ totalCapacity \in 0..MaxTotalCapacity
  /\ freeSlots \in 0..MaxTotalCapacity
  /\ trainSnapshot \in [Trains -> 0..MaxTotalCapacity]
  /\ trainPending \in [Trains -> {"none", "entering", "leaving"}]
  /\ occupied \in [Trains -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ totalCapacity = InitialCapacity
  /\ freeSlots = InitialCapacity
  /\ trainSnapshot = [t \in Trains |-> 0]
  /\ trainPending = [t \in Trains |-> "none"]
  /\ occupied = [t \in Trains |-> FALSE]

\* Read phase: snapshot the register before attempting to claim a slot.
StartEnter(t) ==
  /\ trainPending[t] = "none"
  /\ ~occupied[t]
  /\ trainPending' = [trainPending EXCEPT ![t] = "entering"]
  /\ trainSnapshot' = [trainSnapshot EXCEPT ![t] = freeSlots]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<totalCapacity, freeSlots, occupied>>

\* Swap phase: succeeds only if the register still matches this train's
\* snapshot and a slot remains; otherwise the compare-and-swap has failed
\* and the train must go back and re-read.
CasEnter(t) ==
  /\ trainPending[t] = "entering"
  /\ IF freeSlots = trainSnapshot[t] /\ freeSlots > 0
     THEN /\ freeSlots' = freeSlots - 1
          /\ occupied' = [occupied EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
          /\ trainPending' = [trainPending EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
     ELSE /\ trainPending' = [trainPending EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
          /\ UNCHANGED <<freeSlots, occupied>>
  /\ UNCHANGED <<totalCapacity, trainSnapshot>>

\* Read phase for releasing a slot on the way out of the occupied set.
StartLeave(t) ==
  /\ trainPending[t] = "none"
  /\ occupied[t]
  /\ trainPending' = [trainPending EXCEPT ![t] = "leaving"]
  /\ trainSnapshot' = [trainSnapshot EXCEPT ![t] = freeSlots]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<totalCapacity, freeSlots, occupied>>

\* Swap phase for releasing: same compare-and-swap discipline in reverse.
CasLeave(t) ==
  /\ trainPending[t] = "leaving"
  /\ IF freeSlots = trainSnapshot[t]
     THEN /\ freeSlots' = freeSlots + 1
          /\ occupied' = [occupied EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
          /\ trainPending' = [trainPending EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
     ELSE /\ trainPending' = [trainPending EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
          /\ UNCHANGED <<freeSlots, occupied>>
  /\ UNCHANGED <<totalCapacity, trainSnapshot>>

\* Twist: maintenance opens a new block segment at runtime, growing total
\* capacity and immediately crediting the new spare slot to the register.
ExpandCapacity ==
  /\ totalCapacity < MaxTotalCapacity
  /\ totalCapacity' = totalCapacity + 1
  /\ freeSlots' = freeSlots + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<trainSnapshot, trainPending, occupied>>

\* Twist: maintenance retires a block segment at runtime -- only a spare
\* one, never one a train is actually sitting in -- shrinking total
\* capacity and the register together.
ShrinkCapacity ==
  /\ totalCapacity > 0
  /\ freeSlots > 0
  /\ totalCapacity' = totalCapacity - 1
  /\ freeSlots' = freeSlots - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<trainSnapshot, trainPending, occupied>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains : StartEnter(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : CasEnter(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : StartLeave(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : CasLeave(t)
  \/ ExpandCapacity
  \/ ShrinkCapacity

Fairness ==
  \A t \in Trains :
    /\ WF_vars(CasEnter(t))
    /\ WF_vars(CasLeave(t))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: conservation of spare capacity. The free-slot register never
\* reports more spare capacity than the line's live total actually grants,
\* regardless of how compare-and-swap retries interleave with runtime
\* capacity changes.
CapacityConservation == freeSlots <= totalCapacity

\* LIVENESS: every compare-and-swap attempt a train starts is eventually
\* resolved, one way or the other -- capacity changing at runtime never
\* leaves a train's in-flight attempt stuck forever.
PendingResolves ==
  \A t \in Trains : (trainPending[t] # "none") ~> (trainPending[t] = "none")

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Trains = {t1, t2}
  MaxTotalCapacity = 3
  InitialCapacity = 2
INVARIANT CapacityConservation
PROPERTY PendingResolves
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway line's signalling block system tracks how much spare block
capacity remains in a single shared compare-and-swap register. A train
wanting to enter the occupied block set first snapshots the register's
current value, then attempts an atomic swap that only succeeds if the
register still holds exactly what it last saw and at least one slot is
still spare; if the register has since changed, the compare-and-swap has
failed and the train must go back, take a fresh snapshot, and try again.
Releasing a slot on the way out works the same way in reverse: snapshot,
then attempt the matching swap, retrying on failure. Track maintenance can
also change the line's total capacity while trains are running: it may open
a new block segment at any time, growing total capacity and immediately
crediting the register with the new spare slot, or it may retire a block
segment that is currently spare -- never one a train is actually sitting in
-- shrinking total capacity and the register together. Because the register
and the total capacity can both move while a train's compare-and-swap
attempt is in flight, the discipline of comparing against the exact
snapshot before swapping is what keeps the register's count honest no
matter how capacity changes interleave with train traffic.

The full action set is: StartEnter (a train snapshots the register before
attempting to claim a slot), CasEnter (the train attempts the
compare-and-swap that claims a slot, succeeding only if the register still
matches its snapshot and a slot remains, otherwise failing and forcing a
retry), StartLeave (a train snapshots the register before attempting to
release its slot), CasLeave (the train attempts the compare-and-swap that
releases its slot, succeeding only if the register still matches its
snapshot), ExpandCapacity (maintenance opens a new block segment at
runtime, growing total capacity and the register together), and
ShrinkCapacity (maintenance retires a spare block segment at runtime,
shrinking total capacity and the register together).

SAFETY PROPERTY: spare capacity is conserved -- the free-slot register
never reports more spare capacity than the line's live total actually
grants, no matter how compare-and-swap retries interleave with runtime
capacity changes.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every compare-and-swap attempt a train starts is
eventually resolved, one way or the other, so capacity changing at runtime
never leaves a train's in-flight attempt stuck forever.

---- MODULE W4Od8m7p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants, CrashProne, NoOne, MaxEpoch

ASSUME CrashProne \in Participants
ASSUME NoOne \notin Participants

VARIABLES epoch, owner, authorized, seen, crashed, audit

vars == <<epoch, owner, authorized, seen, crashed, audit>>

\* A compare-and-swap register models the registrar's course-registration
\* ledger: `epoch` is the register's version and `owner` is whichever
\* registration clerk currently holds the pending enrollment transaction.
\* A CAS claim only succeeds when the caller (a) is on the authorized
\* roster and (b) its cached view `seen[p]` still matches the register,
\* i.e. it is neither unauthorized nor stale.  `audit` freezes the roster
\* and staleness gap seen by the *last* successful claim so the invariant
\* can check history without letting a later revocation retroactively
\* poison an already-legitimate past claim.

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ owner = NoOne
    /\ authorized = Participants
    /\ seen = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = FALSE
    /\ audit = [auth |-> Participants, gap |-> 0]

Alive(p) == ~(p = CrashProne /\ crashed)

\* p refreshes its cached view of the register's current epoch.
Read(p) ==
    /\ Alive(p)
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, authorized, crashed, audit>>

\* p attempts a compare-and-swap: only takes effect if p is authorized
\* and p's cached epoch equals the register's current epoch (not stale).
CasClaim(p) ==
    /\ Alive(p)
    /\ p \in authorized
    /\ seen[p] = epoch
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ owner' = p
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![p] = epoch + 1]
    /\ audit' = [auth |-> authorized, gap |-> seen[p] - epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, crashed>>

\* The registrar's office revokes p's standing (e.g. end of add/drop,
\* TA appointment lapses).  Past claims made while p was authorized
\* remain legitimate; only future actions by p are blocked.
Revoke(p) ==
    /\ p \in authorized
    /\ authorized' = authorized \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, seen, crashed, audit>>

\* CrashProne silently crashes: no notification, it simply stops acting.
Crash ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ crashed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, authorized, seen, audit>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Participants: Read(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participants: CasClaim(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participants: Revoke(p)
    \/ Crash

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The register's holder was, at the moment it claimed ownership, both
\* on the authorized roster and non-stale (its compare-and-swap expected
\* value matched the register).  Later revocations cannot retroactively
\* break this because `audit` is a frozen snapshot taken at claim time.
NoUnauthorizedOrStaleAction ==
    /\ (owner = NoOne \/ owner \in audit.auth)
    /\ audit.gap = 0

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedOrStaleAction

CONSTANTS
p1 = p1
p2 = p2
p3 = p3
NoOneVal = NoOneVal
Participants = {p1, p2, p3}
CrashProne = p1
NoOne = NoOneVal
MaxEpoch = 2
nl:
A university's course-registration system lets a small pool of registrar clerks
process pending enrollment transactions for a contested course seat. The seat's
transaction record is guarded by a single compare-and-swap (CAS) register: an
`epoch` counter that increments every time the record is successfully claimed,
and an `owner` field naming whichever clerk currently holds the pending
transaction. To claim the seat, a clerk must first read the register to learn
its current epoch, then submit a CAS operation that only succeeds if (a) the
clerk is still on the registrar's authorized roster and (b) the epoch value
the clerk cached from its last read still matches the register's live epoch.
If either condition fails -- the clerk has been deauthorized, or another
clerk's claim has advanced the epoch in the meantime -- the CAS is rejected
and the clerk must re-read and retry. One clerk is prone to crashing silently:
it can stop responding at any point with no notification to the rest of the
office, after which it can never again read the register or submit a claim.
The registrar's office can also revoke a clerk's authorization at any time
(e.g. when a TA appointment lapses or the add/drop window closes); a clerk's
earlier, already-successful claim stays valid, but the clerk can take no
further action once revoked.

The full action set is: Read (a clerk refreshes its cached view of the
register's epoch), CasClaim (a clerk attempts the compare-and-swap to become
the seat's owner, which only succeeds if it is authorized and its cached
epoch is fresh), Revoke (the registrar's office removes a clerk from the
authorized roster), and Crash (the crash-prone clerk silently stops acting
forever).

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the compare-and-swap register has a current owner, that owner became the owner only while it was on the authorized roster and while its cached epoch exactly matched the register's live epoch, i.e. no unauthorized or stale clerk's claim was ever accepted.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m7p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumOps, SlowOp, MaxEpoch, MaxDelay

Operators == 1..NumOps
NoOne == 0

ASSUME NumOps \in Nat /\ NumOps > 0
ASSUME SlowOp \in Operators

VARIABLES epoch, holder, authorized, view, turn, delay, claim

vars == <<epoch, holder, authorized, view, turn, delay, claim>>

\* A crane-yard control console is granted via a compare-and-swap register:
\* `epoch` versions the register and `holder` is the console currently in
\* control of the quay crane. A dispatcher polls consoles round-robin via
\* `turn` (never more than one console contends at a time), and a claim
\* only succeeds if the console is on the authorized roster and its cached
\* `view` still matches the live epoch (not stale). One console (SlowOp)
\* has mechanical/network lag modeled by a bounded countdown `delay`: it
\* cannot act until the countdown clears, but it always eventually clears
\* -- it is slow, never failed, so the round robin never truly skips it.

NextTurn(p) == IF p = NumOps THEN 1 ELSE p + 1

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ authorized = Operators
    /\ view = [p \in Operators |-> 0]
    /\ turn = 1
    /\ delay = IF SlowOp = 1 THEN MaxDelay ELSE 0
    /\ claim = [view |-> 0, epoch |-> 0]

\* p refreshes its cached view of the register while it holds the turn.
Read(p) ==
    /\ turn = p
    /\ (p = SlowOp => delay = 0)
    /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, authorized, turn, delay, claim>>

\* Mechanical/network latency ticking down for the slow console's turn.
SlowTick ==
    /\ turn = SlowOp
    /\ delay > 0
    /\ delay' = delay - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, authorized, view, turn, claim>>

\* p's compare-and-swap claim: only accepted if it is authorized, its
\* cached view matches the live epoch, and (for the slow console) its
\* latency has cleared. `claim` freezes the exact values compared so the
\* invariant can audit this claim even after later, unrelated Reads
\* update `view[p]` for other purposes. Advances the round-robin turn.
CasClaim(p) ==
    /\ turn = p
    /\ p \in authorized
    /\ view[p] = epoch
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ (p = SlowOp => delay = 0)
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ holder' = p
    /\ turn' = NextTurn(p)
    /\ delay' = IF NextTurn(p) = SlowOp THEN MaxDelay ELSE delay
    /\ claim' = [view |-> view[p], epoch |-> epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, view>>

\* p declines this round (stale view, not authorized, or no interest)
\* and the dispatcher moves the turn on to the next console.
Pass(p) ==
    /\ turn = p
    /\ (p = SlowOp => delay = 0)
    /\ turn' = NextTurn(p)
    /\ delay' = IF NextTurn(p) = SlowOp THEN MaxDelay ELSE delay
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, authorized, view, claim>>

\* The yard office revokes p's authorization; if p currently holds the
\* crane it is dispossessed immediately (no unauthorized holder lingers).
Revoke(p) ==
    /\ p \in authorized
    /\ authorized' = authorized \ {p}
    /\ holder' = IF holder = p THEN NoOne ELSE holder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, view, turn, delay, claim>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Operators: Read(p)
    \/ SlowTick
    \/ \E p \in Operators: CasClaim(p)
    \/ \E p \in Operators: Pass(p)
    \/ \E p \in Operators: Revoke(p)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(SlowTick)
    /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Operators: Read(p))
    /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Operators: CasClaim(p) \/ Pass(p))

\* Whoever currently holds the crane is presently authorized (a revoked
\* console is dispossessed immediately, see Revoke), and the values its
\* compare-and-swap actually compared -- frozen in `claim` at the moment
\* of the grant, immune to later unrelated Reads that keep updating
\* `view` -- really were equal, i.e. no stale claim was ever granted.
NoUnauthorizedOrStaleAction ==
    /\ holder = NoOne \/ holder \in authorized
    /\ holder = NoOne \/ claim.view = claim.epoch

\* The dispatcher's round robin is fair to the slow console: its turn
\* recurs infinitely often, so latency never turns into exclusion.
SlowOpGetsTurn == []<>(turn = SlowOp)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedOrStaleAction
PROPERTY SlowOpGetsTurn

CONSTANTS
NumOps = 3
SlowOp = 1
MaxEpoch = 2
MaxDelay = 2
nl:
A container-ship crane yard has a small bank of operator consoles that can
each request control of a single quay crane. Control is arbitrated by a
compare-and-swap (CAS) register: an `epoch` counter that advances every time
control is granted, and a `holder` field naming the console currently in
control. To avoid a thundering herd of simultaneous claims, the yard's
dispatcher polls the consoles round-robin, one at a time -- only the console
whose turn it currently is may act. When it is a console's turn, it may
first re-read the register to refresh its cached epoch, then attempt a
compare-and-swap claim, which is only granted if the console is on the
yard's authorized roster and its cached epoch still matches the register's
live epoch (i.e. no other console grabbed control in the meantime). If a
console does not wish to claim, or its claim would be rejected, it simply
passes and the dispatcher advances the turn to the next console. One
console has known mechanical and network lag: whenever the turn reaches it,
a bounded countdown must run out before it can read, claim, or even pass --
it is genuinely slow, never failed, and the countdown always eventually
reaches zero so its turn is never skipped or lost. The yard office can also
revoke a console's authorization at any moment; if the revoked console
currently holds the crane, it is dispossessed immediately so no unauthorized
console keeps control.

The full action set is: Read (the console whose turn it is refreshes its
cached view of the register's epoch), SlowTick (the slow console's latency
countdown ticks down by one while it is its turn), CasClaim (the console
whose turn it is submits its compare-and-swap claim, granted only if it is
authorized and its cached epoch is fresh), Pass (the console whose turn it
is declines and the dispatcher advances to the next console), and Revoke
(the yard office removes a console from the authorized roster, immediately
dispossessing it of the crane if it is the current holder).

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the compare-and-swap register has a current holder, that holder is presently on the authorized roster and its cached epoch was exactly one behind the live epoch at the moment it claimed control, so no unauthorized or stale console's claim was ever granted.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: the round-robin dispatcher is fair to the slow console -- its turn comes up infinitely often, so its latency never turns into permanent exclusion from claiming the crane.

---- MODULE W4Od19m8p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Clerks, CrashProne, Slots, Patrons, NoOne, FreeVal, MaxLog

ASSUME CrashProne \in Clerks
ASSUME NoOne \notin Clerks
ASSUME FreeVal \notin Patrons

VARIABLES branchLock, slotLock, occupant, log, crashed

vars == <<branchLock, slotLock, occupant, log, crashed>>

\* A library branch uses hierarchical locking to hand out pickup slots for
\* reserved books: a clerk must first take the coarse branch lock, then a
\* fine per-slot lock, before it may allocate that slot to a patron. `log`
\* is an append-only audit trail of Alloc/Free events. The invariant is a
\* log-contiguity check: for a given slot, two Alloc events may never
\* appear back to back without an intervening Free -- i.e. the slot was
\* never double-allocated to two patrons at once. One clerk can crash
\* silently while still holding locks, which never gets released.

Init ==
    /\ branchLock = NoOne
    /\ slotLock = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]
    /\ occupant = [s \in Slots |-> FreeVal]
    /\ log = <<>>
    /\ crashed = FALSE

Alive(c) == ~(c = CrashProne /\ crashed)

\* A clerk takes the coarse, branch-wide lock (must precede any fine lock).
AcquireBranch(c) ==
    /\ Alive(c)
    /\ branchLock = NoOne
    /\ branchLock' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, occupant, log, crashed>>

\* Only after holding the branch lock may a clerk take a fine slot lock.
AcquireSlot(c, s) ==
    /\ Alive(c)
    /\ branchLock = c
    /\ slotLock[s] = NoOne
    /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<branchLock, occupant, log, crashed>>

\* With the fine lock held and the slot free, allocate it to a patron.
Allocate(c, s, patron) ==
    /\ Alive(c)
    /\ slotLock[s] = c
    /\ occupant[s] = FreeVal
    /\ Len(log) < MaxLog
    /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = patron]
    /\ log' = Append(log, [op |-> "Alloc", slot |-> s])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<branchLock, slotLock, crashed>>

\* With the fine lock held and the slot occupied, cancel the reservation.
Cancel(c, s) ==
    /\ Alive(c)
    /\ slotLock[s] = c
    /\ occupant[s] # FreeVal
    /\ Len(log) < MaxLog
    /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = FreeVal]
    /\ log' = Append(log, [op |-> "Free", slot |-> s])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<branchLock, slotLock, crashed>>

\* A clerk releases a fine lock it holds; once it holds none, it may also
\* release the coarse branch lock in the same step (finish transaction).
Release(c) ==
    /\ Alive(c)
    /\ branchLock = c
    /\ \A s \in Slots: slotLock[s] # c
    /\ branchLock' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, occupant, log, crashed>>

ReleaseSlot(c, s) ==
    /\ Alive(c)
    /\ slotLock[s] = c
    /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<branchLock, occupant, log, crashed>>

\* CrashProne crashes silently, permanently, holding whatever locks it has.
Crash ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ crashed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<branchLock, slotLock, occupant, log>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Clerks: AcquireBranch(c)
    \/ \E c \in Clerks, s \in Slots: AcquireSlot(c, s)
    \/ \E c \in Clerks, s \in Slots, patron \in Patrons: Allocate(c, s, patron)
    \/ \E c \in Clerks, s \in Slots: Cancel(c, s)
    \/ \E c \in Clerks, s \in Slots: ReleaseSlot(c, s)
    \/ \E c \in Clerks: Release(c)
    \/ Crash

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: in the audit log, two Alloc events for the same
\* slot never appear without an intervening Free between them.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A i, j \in 1..Len(log):
        (/\ i < j
         /\ log[i].slot = log[j].slot
         /\ log[i].op = "Alloc"
         /\ log[j].op = "Alloc")
        => \E k \in (i+1)..(j-1): log[k].slot = log[i].slot /\ log[k].op = "Free"

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

CONSTANTS
c1 = c1
c2 = c2
s1 = s1
s2 = s2
q1 = q1
q2 = q2
NoOneVal = NoOneVal
FreeSlotVal = FreeSlotVal
Clerks = {c1, c2}
CrashProne = c1
Slots = {s1, s2}
Patrons = {q1, q2}
NoOne = NoOneVal
FreeVal = FreeSlotVal
MaxLog = 4
nl:
A public library runs a book-reservation system for patrons who want to pick
up a held title from a specific branch. Each branch has a small number of
pickup slots (a physical hold shelf position) that a clerk assigns to a
patron's reservation. Because several clerks can be working the desk at
once, the branch uses hierarchical locking to serialize slot assignment: a
clerk must first take the coarse, branch-wide lock before touching any
individual slot, and only then take the fine-grained lock on the specific
slot it wants to work with. Only with the fine lock held can the clerk
allocate a free slot to a patron, or cancel an existing reservation to free
the slot back up. Every allocation and cancellation is recorded in an
append-only audit log of the branch's activity. One of the clerks is prone
to crashing silently -- mid-shift, without warning, it can simply stop
working, and any locks it was holding at that moment are never released
(they are not recovered in this model).

The full action set is: AcquireBranch (a clerk takes the coarse, branch-wide
lock), AcquireSlot (a clerk holding the branch lock takes the fine lock on a
specific slot), Allocate (a clerk holding a slot's fine lock assigns that
free slot to a patron and logs the assignment), Cancel (a clerk holding a
slot's fine lock frees an occupied slot and logs the cancellation),
ReleaseSlot (a clerk releases a fine lock it holds), Release (a clerk
releases the coarse branch lock once it holds no fine locks), and Crash (the
crash-prone clerk silently and permanently stops acting, forever holding
whatever locks it had).

SAFETY PROPERTY: in the branch's audit log, no slot is ever allocated to a second patron before its prior allocation was logged as cancelled -- the same pickup slot is never double-allocated to two patrons at once.

---- MODULE W4Od9m8p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Feeders, D

ASSUME D \in Nat

VARIABLES dispatchBusy, fineLock, allocated, shed, queue, submitted

vars == <<dispatchBusy, fineLock, allocated, shed, queue, submitted>>

\* A power-grid load shedder uses hierarchical locking: the dispatcher
\* takes a coarse, grid-wide lock before it takes a fine, per-feeder lock
\* and only then may shift a feeder's power between "allocated" (served)
\* and "shed" (curtailed). Each feeder's total demand D is a conserved
\* quantity -- power is only ever moved between allocated and shed, never
\* created or destroyed. A privileged admin can bypass the whole locking
\* protocol for emergency shedding/restoration, but every action, normal
\* or override, must still preserve the same conservation law.

NotQueued(f) == \A i \in 1..Len(queue): queue[i] # f

Init ==
    /\ dispatchBusy = FALSE
    /\ fineLock = [f \in Feeders |-> FALSE]
    /\ allocated = [f \in Feeders |-> D]
    /\ shed = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ submitted = {}

\* A feeder is flagged, at most once ever, as needing dispatcher review.
Submit(f) ==
    /\ f \notin submitted
    /\ NotQueued(f)
    /\ submitted' = submitted \cup {f}
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, f)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispatchBusy, fineLock, allocated, shed>>

\* The dispatcher takes the coarse, grid-wide lock to begin serving the
\* request at the head of the queue.
AcquireDispatch ==
    /\ ~dispatchBusy
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ dispatchBusy' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, allocated, shed, queue, submitted>>

\* Only once the coarse lock is held may the dispatcher take the fine
\* lock on the specific feeder at the head of the queue.
AcquireFineOnHead ==
    /\ dispatchBusy
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ ~fineLock[Head(queue)]
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispatchBusy, allocated, shed, queue, submitted>>

\* With both locks held, curtail one unit of the head feeder's power,
\* moving it from allocated to shed -- the total stays conserved.
ShedHead ==
    /\ dispatchBusy
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ fineLock[Head(queue)]
    /\ allocated[Head(queue)] > 0
    /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = @ - 1]
    /\ shed' = [shed EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispatchBusy, fineLock, queue, submitted>>

\* With both locks held, restore one unit of the head feeder's power,
\* moving it from shed back to allocated -- still conserved.
RestoreHead ==
    /\ dispatchBusy
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ fineLock[Head(queue)]
    /\ shed[Head(queue)] > 0
    /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = @ + 1]
    /\ shed' = [shed EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispatchBusy, fineLock, queue, submitted>>

\* The dispatcher finishes with the head feeder: both locks release and
\* it is popped from the queue, whether or not it was actually adjusted.
Complete ==
    /\ dispatchBusy
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ fineLock[Head(queue)]
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = FALSE]
    /\ dispatchBusy' = FALSE
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocated, shed, submitted>>

\* A privileged admin can shed a feeder in an emergency, bypassing the
\* coarse/fine locking protocol entirely -- but the same conservation
\* bookkeeping applies: the unit moves, it is never simply destroyed.
AdminShed(f) ==
    /\ allocated[f] > 0
    /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
    /\ shed' = [shed EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispatchBusy, fineLock, queue, submitted>>

\* A privileged admin can likewise force an emergency restoration,
\* bypassing the locking protocol, while preserving conservation.
AdminRestore(f) ==
    /\ shed[f] > 0
    /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1]
    /\ shed' = [shed EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispatchBusy, fineLock, queue, submitted>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Feeders: Submit(f)
    \/ AcquireDispatch
    \/ AcquireFineOnHead
    \/ ShedHead
    \/ RestoreHead
    \/ Complete
    \/ \E f \in Feeders: AdminShed(f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders: AdminRestore(f)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(AcquireDispatch)
    /\ WF_vars(AcquireFineOnHead)
    /\ WF_vars(Complete)

\* Conservation: every feeder's allocated and shed power always sums
\* back to its fixed demand D -- power is only ever moved between the
\* two buckets, never created or destroyed, by any action including
\* the admin's override path.
LoadConserved == \A f \in Feeders: allocated[f] + shed[f] = D

\* Liveness: every submitted request is eventually fully processed and
\* the dispatch queue keeps draining back to empty (no request is stuck
\* behind the coarse/fine locking protocol forever).
QueueDrains == []<>(queue = <<>>)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT LoadConserved
PROPERTY QueueDrains

CONSTANTS
f1 = f1
f2 = f2
f3 = f3
Feeders = {f1, f2, f3}
D = 2
nl:
A regional power grid's load shedder manages a handful of feeders that each
carry a fixed amount of demand. When the grid is stressed, the dispatcher
must curtail (shed) some feeders' power and later restore it once conditions
improve. To keep changes serialized and auditable, the dispatcher follows a
hierarchical locking protocol: it must first take a coarse, grid-wide
dispatch lock, and only then take a fine-grained lock on the specific
feeder at the head of its request queue, before it is allowed to shift that
feeder's power between "allocated" (currently served) and "shed" (currently
curtailed). Every unit of a feeder's demand is always accounted for in one
of those two buckets -- power is only ever moved between them, never
created or destroyed. Feeders are flagged for dispatcher review at most
once each; once flagged they join the FIFO request queue and are processed
one at a time. A privileged grid administrator, however, can bypass the
entire coarse/fine locking protocol during an emergency, directly shedding
or restoring a feeder's power immediately -- but even the admin's override
must obey the same conservation bookkeeping as the normal path.

The full action set is: Submit (a feeder is flagged for dispatcher review
and joins the request queue, at most once per feeder), AcquireDispatch (the
dispatcher takes the coarse, grid-wide lock to begin serving the queue's
head), AcquireFineOnHead (the dispatcher takes the fine lock on the
specific feeder at the head of the queue), ShedHead (with both locks held,
one unit of the head feeder's power moves from allocated to shed),
RestoreHead (with both locks held, one unit of the head feeder's power
moves from shed back to allocated), Complete (the dispatcher releases both
locks and pops the head feeder off the queue, finishing its review),
AdminShed (the privileged admin sheds one unit of any feeder's power
immediately, without acquiring any lock), and AdminRestore (the privileged
admin restores one unit of any feeder's power immediately, without
acquiring any lock).

SAFETY PROPERTY: for every feeder, its allocated power plus its shed power always equals its fixed total demand -- no unit of power is ever created or destroyed by any action, dispatcher-mediated or admin override alike.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every feeder flagged for review is eventually fully processed by the dispatcher, so the request queue keeps draining back to empty rather than leaving any request stuck behind the locking protocol forever.

---- MODULE W4Od19m7p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, MaxCopies, InitialCopies, MaxVersion

ASSUME InitialCopies \in 0..MaxCopies

VARIABLES version, count, localVersion, localCount, pendingOp, casAuditV

vars == <<version, count, localVersion, localCount, pendingOp, casAuditV>>

\* Two independent library front-ends (e.g. two branch kiosks) share one
\* central pool of copies for a popular title, guarded by a single
\* compare-and-swap register: `version` and `count` are the pool's live
\* state. Each front-end caches its own last-read (localVersion,
\* localCount) and stages an intended reserve/return in `pendingOp`
\* before attempting to commit. A commit only takes effect if the
\* front-end's cached version still matches the live version -- otherwise
\* it must re-Read and retry -- which is exactly what prevents a lost
\* update: an instance can never blindly overwrite the pool with a delta
\* computed from a stale snapshot.

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ count = InitialCopies
    /\ localVersion = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ localCount = [i \in Instances |-> InitialCopies]
    /\ pendingOp = [i \in Instances |-> "none"]
    /\ casAuditV = [exp |-> 0, live |-> 0]

\* i refreshes its cached snapshot of the shared pool.
Read(i) ==
    /\ localVersion' = [localVersion EXCEPT ![i] = version]
    /\ localCount' = [localCount EXCEPT ![i] = count]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, count, pendingOp, casAuditV>>

\* i stages an intent to reserve a copy, based on its (possibly stale)
\* cached view showing a copy available.
StartReserve(i) ==
    /\ pendingOp[i] = "none"
    /\ localCount[i] > 0
    /\ pendingOp' = [pendingOp EXCEPT ![i] = "reserve"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, count, localVersion, localCount, casAuditV>>

\* i stages an intent to return a copy it previously reserved.
StartReturn(i) ==
    /\ pendingOp[i] = "none"
    /\ pendingOp' = [pendingOp EXCEPT ![i] = "return"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, count, localVersion, localCount, casAuditV>>

\* i abandons a staged intent without committing (e.g. it changed its
\* mind, or gives up retrying after repeated conflicts).
CancelPending(i) ==
    /\ pendingOp[i] # "none"
    /\ pendingOp' = [pendingOp EXCEPT ![i] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, count, localVersion, localCount, casAuditV>>

\* i attempts to commit its staged delta via compare-and-swap: the new
\* pool value is computed from i's *cached* snapshot (as a real CAS
\* register commits a whole new value, not a live in-place adjustment),
\* and the commit only takes effect if i's cached version still matches
\* the pool's live version. `casAuditV` freezes exactly what was
\* compared so the invariant can audit it: if a stale commit ever slips
\* through, the frozen expected/live pair will disagree.
CommitCas(i) ==
    /\ pendingOp[i] # "none"
    /\ localVersion[i] = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ LET newCount == IF pendingOp[i] = "reserve"
                        THEN localCount[i] - 1
                        ELSE localCount[i] + 1
       IN  /\ newCount \in 0..MaxCopies
           /\ count' = newCount
           /\ version' = version + 1
           /\ localVersion' = [localVersion EXCEPT ![i] = version + 1]
           /\ localCount' = [localCount EXCEPT ![i] = newCount]
    /\ pendingOp' = [pendingOp EXCEPT ![i] = "none"]
    /\ casAuditV' = [exp |-> localVersion[i], live |-> version]

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances: Read(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances: StartReserve(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances: StartReturn(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances: CancelPending(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances: CommitCas(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost update: every commit's compare-and-swap really did compare
\* equal values -- the committing instance's cached version genuinely
\* matched the pool's live version at the moment it wrote, so its
\* cached (and hence its computed delta) was never stale, and no other
\* instance's concurrent commit was ever silently overwritten.
NoLostUpdate == casAuditV.exp = casAuditV.live

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate

CONSTANTS
a = a
b = b
Instances = {a, b}
MaxCopies = 3
InitialCopies = 2
MaxVersion = 4
nl:
A library system runs two independent front-end kiosks (for example, two
different branch terminals, or a web checkout terminal and an in-person
desk terminal) that both let patrons reserve or return copies of the same
popular title. Rather than each kiosk keeping its own inventory, they share
a single central pool of available copies, guarded by a compare-and-swap
(CAS) register: a `version` counter and a `count` of copies currently
available. Each kiosk keeps its own cached snapshot of the pool (its last
observed version and count) and, when a patron wants to reserve or return a
copy, stages that intent locally before attempting to commit. Committing is
a genuine compare-and-swap: the kiosk computes what it believes the new
count should be from its own cached snapshot, then submits that new value
only if its cached version still matches the pool's live version. If
another kiosk has committed a change in the meantime, the version will have
moved on, the compare-and-swap is rejected, and the kiosk must re-read the
pool and retry -- which is exactly what stops one kiosk's write from
silently clobbering (losing) the other kiosk's concurrent update.

The full action set is: Read (a kiosk refreshes its cached version and
count from the shared pool), StartReserve (a kiosk stages an intent to
reserve a copy, based on its cached view showing one available),
StartReturn (a kiosk stages an intent to return a previously reserved
copy), CancelPending (a kiosk abandons a staged intent without
committing), and CommitCas (a kiosk attempts to commit its staged delta,
which only succeeds if its cached version still matches the pool's live
version, after which the pool's version and count both advance).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every successful compare-and-swap commit really did compare a kiosk's cached version against a pool version that genuinely matched at that moment, so no kiosk's update to the shared copy pool is ever silently lost to a concurrent commit from the other kiosk.

---- MODULE W4Od17m6p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Handlers, Bags, MaxLeaseTicks

NoOne == "NoOne"

VARIABLES leaseHolder, ticksLeft, loadCount, adminOverridden

vars == <<leaseHolder, ticksLeft, loadCount, adminOverridden>>

\* An airport baggage router hands each bag off to a handler under a
\* time-bound lease: a handler must hold a bag's lease before it may
\* perform the irreversible act of loading it onto its outbound cart.
\* If a handler never acts, the lease's countdown reaches zero and the
\* lease is reclaimed so another handler can try. `loadCount` records how
\* many times a bag has actually been loaded -- the property under test
\* is that this can never exceed one, even across lease handoffs and the
\* privileged admin override that can force a load immediately.

Init ==
    /\ leaseHolder = [b \in Bags |-> NoOne]
    /\ ticksLeft = [b \in Bags |-> 0]
    /\ loadCount = [b \in Bags |-> 0]
    /\ adminOverridden = [b \in Bags |-> FALSE]

\* h takes the lease on an unclaimed, not-yet-loaded bag.
AcquireLease(h, b) ==
    /\ leaseHolder[b] = NoOne
    /\ loadCount[b] = 0
    /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![b] = h]
    /\ ticksLeft' = [ticksLeft EXCEPT ![b] = MaxLeaseTicks]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loadCount, adminOverridden>>

\* Time passes on a held, not-yet-loaded bag's lease.
Tick(b) ==
    /\ leaseHolder[b] # NoOne
    /\ loadCount[b] = 0
    /\ ticksLeft[b] > 0
    /\ ticksLeft' = [ticksLeft EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseHolder, loadCount, adminOverridden>>

\* The lease expires because its holder never loaded the bag in time;
\* it is reclaimed so a different handler can take over.
ExpireLease(b) ==
    /\ leaseHolder[b] # NoOne
    /\ loadCount[b] = 0
    /\ ticksLeft[b] = 0
    /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![b] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ticksLeft, loadCount, adminOverridden>>

\* The lease holder performs the irreversible load. Only possible once
\* per bag: the loadCount[b] = 0 guard is exactly what "at most once"
\* depends on here.
LoadBag(h, b) ==
    /\ leaseHolder[b] = h
    /\ loadCount[b] = 0
    /\ loadCount' = [loadCount EXCEPT ![b] = 1]
    /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![b] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ticksLeft, adminOverridden>>

\* A privileged supervisor can force the irreversible load through
\* immediately, bypassing the whole lease-acquisition protocol -- but
\* it is still bound by the very same "not already loaded" guard.
AdminForceLoad(b) ==
    /\ loadCount[b] = 0
    /\ loadCount' = [loadCount EXCEPT ![b] = 1]
    /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![b] = NoOne]
    /\ adminOverridden' = [adminOverridden EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ticksLeft>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Handlers, b \in Bags: AcquireLease(h, b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags: Tick(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags: ExpireLease(b)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers, b \in Bags: LoadBag(h, b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags: AdminForceLoad(b)

\* Fairness is scoped per bag so every individual bag is guaranteed to
\* make progress, not just the aggregate action class. LoadBag needs
\* *strong* fairness: acquiring and losing a lease can repeatedly toggle
\* it between enabled and disabled, so only "enabled infinitely often"
\* (not "enabled continuously") can be assumed of it.
Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A b \in Bags:
         /\ WF_vars(\E h \in Handlers: AcquireLease(h, b))
         /\ WF_vars(Tick(b))
         /\ WF_vars(ExpireLease(b))
         /\ SF_vars(\E h \in Handlers: LoadBag(h, b))

\* The irreversible load happens at most once per bag, whether it comes
\* through the normal lease protocol or the admin's override path.
AtMostOnceLoaded == \A b \in Bags: loadCount[b] <= 1

\* Liveness: every bag is eventually, irreversibly loaded exactly once
\* -- lease expiry and handoff never leave a bag stuck forever.
AllBagsLoaded == \A b \in Bags: loadCount[b] = 1
EventuallyAllLoaded == <>AllBagsLoaded

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT AtMostOnceLoaded
PROPERTY EventuallyAllLoaded
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

CONSTANTS
h1 = h1
h2 = h2
b1 = b1
b2 = b2
Handlers = {h1, h2}
Bags = {b1, b2}
MaxLeaseTicks = 2
nl:
An airport's baggage router hands off each bag to one of a small pool of
handling robots for final routing. Before a handler may perform the
irreversible act of loading a bag onto its outbound cart (once loaded, the
bag cannot be unloaded or reloaded through this system), it must first hold
a time-bound lease on that bag. A lease is granted to whichever handler
claims an unclaimed, not-yet-loaded bag, and it comes with a countdown: if
the holding handler never gets around to loading the bag before the
countdown reaches zero, the lease expires and is reclaimed so a different
handler can take over. A privileged ramp supervisor can also force a bag's
load through immediately, bypassing the entire lease-acquisition dance --
useful during a schedule crunch -- but even that override is still subject
to the same rule that a bag can only ever be loaded once.

The full action set is: AcquireLease (a handler claims the lease on an
unclaimed, unloaded bag), Tick (time passes on a held bag's lease
countdown), ExpireLease (a bag's lease countdown reaches zero and is
reclaimed because its holder never loaded it), LoadBag (the current lease
holder performs the irreversible load, which is only possible once per
bag), and AdminForceLoad (the privileged supervisor forces the irreversible
load through immediately, bypassing the lease protocol, still gated by the
same not-already-loaded check).

SAFETY PROPERTY: for every bag, the irreversible load action happens at most once, whether it is performed by the handler currently holding the lease or forced through by the supervisor's override.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bag is eventually loaded exactly once -- the lease-expiry and re-acquisition protocol guarantees no bag is left stuck in limbo forever, even if whichever handler first claims it never gets around to loading it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m8p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS ControlInstances, Blocks, Trains, Capacity

NoOne == "NoOne"

VARIABLES zoneLock, blockLock, presence

vars == <<zoneLock, blockLock, presence>>

\* Two independent signalling control centers (e.g. a north and a south
\* control room) share one pool of track blocks in a shared interlocking
\* zone. Hierarchical locking serializes entry: a control center must
\* take the coarse, zone-wide lock before taking a fine lock on a
\* specific block, and only then may it admit or release a train from
\* that block. Every block has a fixed physical capacity; the property
\* under test is that no block ever holds more trains than it can
\* physically hold, no matter which of the two instances is driving.

Init ==
    /\ zoneLock = NoOne
    /\ blockLock = [b \in Blocks |-> NoOne]
    /\ presence = [b \in Blocks |-> {}]

InAnyBlock(tr) == \E b \in Blocks: tr \in presence[b]

\* A control instance takes the coarse, zone-wide lock.
AcquireZone(inst) ==
    /\ zoneLock = NoOne
    /\ zoneLock' = inst
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockLock, presence>>

\* Only while holding the zone lock, and holding no other block's fine
\* lock, may an instance take a specific block's fine lock.
AcquireBlock(inst, b) ==
    /\ zoneLock = inst
    /\ blockLock[b] = NoOne
    /\ \A b2 \in Blocks: blockLock[b2] # inst
    /\ blockLock' = [blockLock EXCEPT ![b] = inst]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, presence>>

\* With the block's fine lock held, admit a train not already present
\* in any block, provided the block is under its physical capacity.
Admit(inst, b, tr) ==
    /\ blockLock[b] = inst
    /\ ~InAnyBlock(tr)
    /\ Cardinality(presence[b]) < Capacity
    /\ presence' = [presence EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {tr}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, blockLock>>

\* With the block's fine lock held, a present train departs the block.
Depart(inst, b, tr) ==
    /\ blockLock[b] = inst
    /\ tr \in presence[b]
    /\ presence' = [presence EXCEPT ![b] = @ \ {tr}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, blockLock>>

\* The instance releases the fine lock it holds on a block.
ReleaseBlock(inst, b) ==
    /\ blockLock[b] = inst
    /\ blockLock' = [blockLock EXCEPT ![b] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, presence>>

\* Once holding no block locks, the instance releases the zone lock.
ReleaseZone(inst) ==
    /\ zoneLock = inst
    /\ \A b \in Blocks: blockLock[b] # inst
    /\ zoneLock' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockLock, presence>>

Next ==
    \/ \E inst \in ControlInstances: AcquireZone(inst)
    \/ \E inst \in ControlInstances, b \in Blocks: AcquireBlock(inst, b)
    \/ \E inst \in ControlInstances, b \in Blocks, tr \in Trains: Admit(inst, b, tr)
    \/ \E inst \in ControlInstances, b \in Blocks, tr \in Trains: Depart(inst, b, tr)
    \/ \E inst \in ControlInstances, b \in Blocks: ReleaseBlock(inst, b)
    \/ \E inst \in ControlInstances: ReleaseZone(inst)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity is never exceeded, whichever of the two shared
\* control instances most recently admitted a train into the block.
CapacityRespected == \A b \in Blocks: Cardinality(presence[b]) <= Capacity

====
