SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

CONSTANTS
n = n
s = s
blk1 = blk1
blk2 = blk2
t1 = t1
t2 = t2
t3 = t3
ControlInstances = {n, s}
Blocks = {blk1, blk2}
Trains = {t1, t2, t3}
Capacity = 2
nl:
A subway system's signalling infrastructure includes a shared interlocking
zone -- a junction area used by trains arriving from two different lines --
managed jointly by two independent signalling control centers, a north
control room and a south control room. Rather than each control room owning
a separate copy of the junction's track blocks, both share exactly one pool
of blocks and must coordinate access to it. They do so with hierarchical
locking: a control room must first take the coarse, zone-wide lock covering
the whole shared junction before it may take a fine-grained lock on any
individual block within it, and only while holding a block's fine lock may
it admit a train into that block or let one depart. Each block has a fixed
physical capacity (how many trains can physically fit on that stretch of
track at once), and a train can only ever be present in one block at a
time.

The full action set is: AcquireZone (a control instance takes the coarse,
zone-wide lock), AcquireBlock (a control instance holding the zone lock,
and holding no other block's fine lock, takes the fine lock on a specific
block), Admit (with a block's fine lock held, a train not already present
anywhere in the zone is admitted into that block, provided it is under
capacity), Depart (with a block's fine lock held, a present train leaves
the block), ReleaseBlock (the instance releases the fine lock it holds on a
block), and ReleaseZone (once holding no block locks, the instance releases
the zone-wide lock).

SAFETY PROPERTY: no track block in the shared interlocking zone ever holds more trains than its fixed physical capacity, regardless of which of the two independent control centers most recently admitted a train into it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m3p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RobotIds, MaxTerm

ASSUME MaxTerm \in Nat /\ MaxTerm > 0

NoOne == "NoOne"

VARIABLES active, leader, term, holder

vars == <<active, leader, term, holder>>

\* A warehouse robot fleet elects a leader (with failover on leader
\* loss) to arbitrate a single critical resource, e.g. a narrow charging
\* dock only one robot can occupy at a time. `active` is the currently
\* participating fleet -- robots can join or leave at runtime, so the
\* pool of candidates the leader is drawn from changes size dynamically.
\* Only the current leader may ever hold the resource; a vacancy (no
\* leader) always precedes any new election, which is exactly what
\* keeps mutual exclusion intact across leadership handoffs.

Init ==
    /\ active = {}
    /\ leader = NoOne
    /\ term = 0
    /\ holder = NoOne

\* A robot joins the active fleet -- the pool of election candidates
\* grows at runtime.
Join(r) ==
    /\ r \notin active
    /\ active' = active \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, holder>>

\* A non-leader robot leaves the active fleet -- the pool shrinks at
\* runtime. (A leaving leader is handled separately, see LeaderFails.)
Leave(r) ==
    /\ r \in active
    /\ r # leader
    /\ active' = active \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, holder>>

\* The current leader fails and drops out of the fleet. Any resource it
\* was holding is released immediately -- no stale holder ever lingers
\* past its leader's failure, which is exactly what keeps the mutual
\* exclusion invariant meaningful through failover.
LeaderFails ==
    /\ leader # NoOne
    /\ active' = active \ {leader}
    /\ holder' = IF holder = leader THEN NoOne ELSE holder
    /\ leader' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term>>

\* With no current leader, a new leader is elected from the active
\* fleet and the term advances (wrapping around a small bound so the
\* state space stays finite -- the absolute term number carries no
\* meaning here beyond "newer than the last one"). Requiring a vacancy
\* first is what prevents two simultaneous "authorities" (a stale old
\* leader plus a freshly elected new one) from ever coexisting.
Elect(r) ==
    /\ leader = NoOne
    /\ r \in active
    /\ leader' = r
    /\ term' = IF term < MaxTerm THEN term + 1 ELSE 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, holder>>

\* Only the current leader may take hold of the critical resource.
Acquire ==
    /\ leader # NoOne
    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ holder' = leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, leader, term>>

\* The current holder releases the critical resource.
Release ==
    /\ holder # NoOne
    /\ holder' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, leader, term>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in RobotIds: Join(r)
    \/ \E r \in RobotIds: Leave(r)
    \/ LeaderFails
    \/ \E r \in RobotIds: Elect(r)
    \/ Acquire
    \/ Release

\* Election needs *strong* fairness: the active fleet can flap (a robot
\* joining and leaving repeatedly), so an election opportunity may only
\* be enabled intermittently rather than continuously -- strong
\* fairness is what still guarantees it isn't dodged forever.
Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ SF_vars(\E r \in RobotIds: Elect(r))

\* Mutual exclusion: the critical resource is never held by anyone
\* other than the currently elected leader -- no stale or rival
\* authority ever gets to occupy it.
MutualExclusion == holder = NoOne \/ holder = leader

\* Liveness: if the fleet is repeatedly non-empty over time, a leader is
\* repeatedly (re-)elected over time too -- a vacancy caused by failover
\* is never left standing forever as long as the fleet keeps coming
\* back. (A fleet that empties out once and for all is, unavoidably,
\* exempt -- there is no one left to elect.)
FleetRecoversLeader == []<>(active # {}) => []<>(leader # NoOne)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY FleetRecoversLeader
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

CONSTANTS
r1 = r1
r2 = r2
r3 = r3
RobotIds = {r1, r2, r3}
MaxTerm = 3
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a single critical resource -- for instance, a
narrow charging dock that physically fits only one robot at a time. Rather
than hard-coding a fixed roster, the fleet is dynamic: robots can join the
active pool when they power on and come online, and can leave it when they
power down or roll off for maintenance, so the size of the pool that can
compete for leadership changes at runtime. Access to the resource is
arbitrated through leader election with failover: at any moment either
there is no leader (a vacancy) or there is exactly one, and only the
current leader is ever allowed to take hold of the resource. If the current
leader itself fails and drops out of the active pool, the resource it was
holding is released immediately and the fleet is left with a vacancy until
a new leader is elected from whichever robots are active at that point.

The full action set is: Join (a robot joins the active fleet), Leave (a
non-leader robot leaves the active fleet), LeaderFails (the current leader
fails, drops out of the active fleet, and releases the resource if it was
holding it), Elect (with no current leader, a new leader is chosen from the
active fleet and the term advances), Acquire (the current leader takes hold
of the critical resource), and Release (the current holder releases the
critical resource).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the critical resource is never held by any robot other than the currently elected leader -- a stale or rival authority can never occupy it alongside or instead of the true leader.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: if the active fleet is repeatedly non-empty over the fleet's lifetime, then it repeatedly recovers a leader too -- a vacancy left by a leader's failure never stands forever as long as the fleet keeps coming back (a fleet that empties out permanently is, unavoidably, the one case with no one left to elect).
